La mayoría de las encuestas dan al bloque de Netanyahu entre 50 y 51 escaños, y a la oposición judía, entre 52 y 53. Solo una lo sitúa al filo de la mayoría de 61. Las dos listas árabes, impulsadas por una participación del 77,7%, la más alta desde 2001, se convierten así en la llave del próximo Gobierno, con 17 escaños según el Canal 13. items.title: Ecobank Group profit before tax hits US$737 million for first nine months of 2026
items.description: Ecobank Group has reported continued growth in its financial results for the first nine months of 2026, despite an operating environment characterised by inflationary pressures, foreign exchange volatility and slower economic activity in parts of Africa. The Group reported profit before tax of US$737 million, up 12% year-on-year, while net revenue increased 12% to US$2.0 billion. Growth was supported by a continued focus on operational efficiency, customer deposit mobilisation, technology investments and disciplined execution of the Group’s Growth, Transformation and Returns (GTR) strategy. Ecobank continued to strengthen its balance sheet, with customer deposits growing to US$27.5 billion while maintaining a strong liquidity and capital position. The Group’s cost-to-income ratio improved to 47.8%, ahead of its target range of 48% to 50%, reflecting ongoing efficiency initiatives across the business. Performance was supported by Ecobank’s diversified business model and geographic footprint. Central, Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) delivered a 20% increase in profit before tax, while Anglophone West Africa (AWA) recorded 10% growth, offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria. These results demonstrate the resilience of the group’s franchise across multiple markets. The Group also continued to benefit from balanced contributions from its corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking businesses. Ecobank’s payments and digital businesses remained important growth drivers. Payment revenue increased by 9%, supported by sustained investment in technology platforms and digital capabilities designed to enhance customer experience and expand financial inclusion across Africa. Key highlights Net revenue increased 12% year-on-year to US$2 billion, while profit before tax increased 12% year-on-year to US$737 million, demonstrating strong business momentum despite macroeconomic and geopolitical headwinds. Operational efficiency continued to improve, with the cost-to-income ratio reaching 47.8%, ahead of the Group’s 2026 target range. Customer deposits increased 14% year-on-year to US$27.5 billion, demonstrating strong customer confidence and the strength of Ecobank’s deposit franchise. Performance remained broadly diversified across regions and businesses, with CESA increasing profit before tax by 20% and AWA by 10%, complemented by contributions from both corporate and investment banking and commercial and consumer banking. Group CEO on financial performance According to Group CEO Jeremy Awori, “We achieved a profit before tax of $737 million, an increase of 12% year-on-year, and a return on tangible equity of 24.9%. Net revenue also grew by 12%, reaching $2.0 billion.” He added that “Our Growth, Transformation, and Returns strategy is clearly reflected in our efficiency and franchise performance. He also stated that the Group’s cost-to-income ratio was 47.8%, ahead of its 2026 target range of 48% to 50%. Customer deposits rose 14% to $27.5 billion, with current and savings accounts accounting for 85% of the total. “This reflects the confidence and trust our customers have in us and in using us for their day-to-day banking. This growth has helped mitigate margin pressure from the rate-easing cycle in our markets, lifting net interest income by 12%. Payment revenue also rose 9%, supported by our continued investment in technology and digital platforms. The strength of our diversified business model was evident as profit before tax increased by 20% in Central Eastern and Southern Africa (CESA) and by 10% in Anglophone West Africa (AWA), offsetting softer results in Francophone West Africa (UEMOA) and Nigeria,” he explained. Awori added, “Our non-performing loan (NPL) ratio remained broadly stable during the quarter at 7.5%, which is within our 2026 target range of 6% to 8%, reflecting continued discipline in portfolio and risk management.” In conclusion, Awori remarked, “Energy prices, inflation, and foreign exchange volatility are real risks as we move through the remainder of the year. However, our strong deposit base, liquidity and capital position, combined with our new products and propositions, position us well to drive further growth while maintaining a disciplined approach to risk. We remain on track to meet our 2026 targets. I want to thank the Ecobank team for their dedication to serving our customers every day.” Continued momentum beyond financial performance During the quarter, Ecobank continued to strengthen its international presence through the opening of its new Beijing Representative Office premises and the signing of a protocol with the Chinese Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS). The Group also concluded its Ecobank@40 celebrations with a US$2.6 billion commitment aimed at supporting women-owned businesses and agriculture across Africa. Ecobank’s leadership was further recognised at the Global Finance Awards during the World Bank and IMF Meetings, where the Group received prestigious distinctions, including Best Bank in Africa 2026 and World’s Best Frontier Markets Bank 2026. These achievements underscore Ecobank’s continued commitment to innovation, customer service and sustainable growth across the continent.

Kwesi Yankah: ‘Awengaa’ teacher on the loose as women march in protest
items.description: Two years ago, my sleep was disturbed by news of child rapists on the prowl disguised as customary rites. Here they come again this time in partisan costume. Listen to an excerpt from my write-up, 2024, on ‘Awengaa:’ We were careful those days in Duakwa not to be shamed and mocked as ‘Awengaa.’ A thirty-year-old man who had ‘slept’ with an underage girl; he was Awengaa. A forty-year-old having his way with a class four girl; they tagged him ‘Awengaa.’ He had grey hair, and the girl was only eight: Awengaa. So young girls took to their heels when they saw him from afar: ‘they say if you cross his red line, hmmmm.’ Little girls would giggle and scamper off. In cases where the victim was really a baby, the idiom carried a literal meaning: Awengaa: ‘a predator of crying babies.’ Paedophile! “It was a virtual taboo, a serious cultural breach. If caught, the offender would be paraded in the streets, gong gong, with songs of shame and boos trailing: ‘Waware ne ba, Akwasi,’ the song stigmatising the bad man. ‘He has slept with a girl young enough to be his daughter.’ The publicity was to caution the innocent one who might mistakenly make an Awengaa’s home a temporary day care: ‘Look after my girl-child until I return from the farm.’ Times have changed. The notorious Awengaa this time may be Your beloved Teacher Mensah;’ worse still, Master Mensah himself: the Big Boss among the Teachers. In Ogyakromian lingo, the Big man ‘himself himself;’ the alpha and omega! The school’s ultimate role model caught pants down! So then it could no longer be said of Master: ‘Suffer the children to come unto Master, for they shall be safe.’Master is no longer a safe refuge! No longer a Head Master, but a Bad Master. Under his care, he could give the kids a bad touch when nobody is watching, or lure them to a secret site and defile them. Not in those days; not Teacher Biney, not Teacher Ansah. Whether in primary or high school, the pattern gets worse and worse: mmɔndaa at school—rape, defilement, having your way with little school girls. The situation gets uglier when higher school authorities summon an Awengaa for sanctions. Hear the authorities’ sanctions for child rape: ‘Ladies and gentlemen, as punishment for this serious offence, we have decided to transfer Awengaa to another school… this time to a village without electricity!’ Here, the announced penalty is indeed a certificate of merit: a handshake meant to help Awengaa spread the virus in darkness! Other times, Awengaa himself, once caught and suspended, may decide to leave the classroom voluntarily and go to the safe haven of politics, where no one checks backgrounds. If he has failed as a custodian of underage girls, he may be a great Party ‘Chaaarman!’ Elsewhere, a concerned local community upset by the soft penalty may take a landmark decision: ‘Henceforth, all authorities that give any Awengaa a slap on the wrist, instead of a harsh penalty, shall be declared as suspects themselves. They are all Awengaa…. Awengaa sɔɔɔn: Monkye wɔn! So why wasn’t the long delay after the Obuasi scandal surprising? Remember the calendar of events. April 2025: suspicion that the new Headmaster was indeed a Bad Master; February 2026: a formal petition about him is sent to authorities.March: multiple reports about him; July/August: concerned old students petition authorities; August: students go on a rampage on campus and attack the ‘Bad Master.’ Education Ministry launches an Inquiry; on 14 October, Obuasi Awengaa is suspended…and an eternal CID probe begins. By the end of October, the everlasting probe continues with no end in sight. Since 2025, Awengaa has allegedly defiled several girls, hiding beneath his zip a total of 19 victims. Pɔr pɔr pɔr pɔr19; enough for a Guinness Book of Awengaa, or a Ballon d’Or! Surprisingly, Ghana, your beloved country, is mute, arms folded! No word on the investigations, not even an invite like, ‘Bad Master, please see the police.’ Madam Lydia Donkor, Head of CID. We haven’t seen your ‘red eyes’ yet. Where is your magic that swiftly brought down Salomey from Techiman while investigating ‘Ghana Jollof ‘? Remember, that lady, Salomey, had three kids but found herself painfully separated from them by 370 kilometres. Despite the distance, the arrest was swift. What then slows down the arrest of a suspected paedophile? Auntie Lydia, Salomey’s youngest child was only five years. You yourself are a mother of twins. That lady was in remand for a month without her kids; and kids without mummy for a month. In the case of the rape victims in Obuasi, while they and their families reel in pain, the predator is comfortably at rest, not on remand, nor on bail, nor in jail, nor in court. Is the state pampering a paedophile? Auntie Lydia, Aww! Asɛm yi yɛ yaw! The rape victims could be the future of your own twin girls or anybody’s daughters desperately crying for swift justice. Yet your outfit is not in a hurry, and eyebrows are raised. So then, our verdict. The education authorities who have been spectators for 16 months, pampering a suspected paedophile: A case to answer. Director CID, seeing no evil, hearing no evil; Mother of twin girls, there is a case to answer. Venue? The bar of public opinion. Then this bombshell that belittles all else. The case of an apolitical activist who, on camera, plays down the rape case in a blatant self-confession. Hear his words: ‘Why are we behaving as if it is not normal to rape? How many of you have never raped a woman?” Those were the words of a ruling-party communicator. So far, no denial, no condemnation; no distancing. The loud silence simply means, ‘Say it Loud, Brother! Rape is normal.’ It’s quite clear this frightening rape case has taken a political turn. The suspect being a party activist, a guilty verdict may give his party the dreaded name: Awengaa People’s Party. The Opposition may be waiting to justify the name change, so they’ll keep pussyfooting until Harmattan winds blow the case away. If the Awengaa suspect is proven innocent, Tweaaa, I will join the all-night Miracle service. Are we sacrificing our kids’ future for political power? Oh my God! Where are the Mrs Mary Grants of yesteryear? Our beloved Jane Naana? The majority women’s caucus? We need words from within that call the Reset team to order, and simply plead: ‘JM, please don’t let down your children.’ The last time I heard from the Ministry of Gender and Children’s Protection, the Minister on TV was speaking English in the future tense! And Haruna, the Minister for Education: English grammar in the future tense. The Vice Presidency? English grammar in the future tense. Happily, I hear the bells ringing for a peaceful demo this week. The red eyes of women activists seek Justice for our kids In the meantime, please keep our girl kids off the streets. Awengaa Teacher is still at large. ******* The writer can be contacted via email at kyankah@ashesi.edu.gh

items.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m at New York auction
items.description: The mounted skeleton of a newly identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m). Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby’s in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus. The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction follows Sotheby’s sale of a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July. The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly. Sotheby’s described Jodi as an “excellent exhibition-ready” skeleton with about 191 fossil-bone elements and a “beautifully preserved, virtually complete skull”. The auction house added that the Nanotyrannus is “one of only three such skeletons known to science”. Sotheby’s said the specimen is the first to come to market since US researchers confirmed the genus’s existence last October. Sotheby’s has not disclosed the identity of the buyer, who won after a thrilling 12-minute auction between six interested parties. It becomes the second-most valuable dinosaur fossil ever sold, behind Gus. The third-most valuable was a Stegosaurus named Apex, which Sotheby’s sold in July 2024 for $44.6m. Megan Jacobs, a palaeontologist at the University of Portsmouth, told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Tuesday that Nanotyrannus “was for a very long time believed to be sort of a teenager of T. rex”. “But it’s a lot smaller and its a lot more gracile. So it’s very sort-of sleek, slender, [with] blade-like teeth for slicing through meat,” Jacobs said. Tyrannosaurus rex and Nanotyrannus lived alongside one another during the same geological period approximately 67 million years ago. Jodi was initially exhibited as a juvenile T. rex at London’s Frieze Masters international art fair in October 2023, before scientists classified the Nanotyrannus genus. Rancher Jodi Pierson discovered the skeleton on her land in Montana, in the Hell Creek Formation, a heavily studied geological site. Commercial palaeontologist Clayton Phipps later excavated it. Phipps also discovered the famous “Duelling Dinosaurs” fossil. That specimen, showing the remains of a Nanotyrannus and Triceratops apparently in combat, was found eight miles (13km) from Jodi in 2006. The “Duelling Dinosaurs” discovery became crucial to the research published by Lindsay Zanno and James Napoli that classified Nanotyrannus as separate from T. rex. Their paper ended decades of debate over whether the dinosaurs were distinct. The auction of Jodi comes as some scientists warn that auctions could herald a new era in fossil collecting by the ultra-rich. Researchers told the BBC after the sale of Gus that such remains should be exhibited in public spaces where they can be more freely studied. Prof Steve Brusatte, a palaeontologist at the University of Edinburgh and consultant on the Jurassic Park films, told BBC World Service’s What in the World programme in July that the T. rex’s auction was “concerning”. “I don’t know of any museum or university that can afford a price tag like that,” he said. “Imagine if the Mona Lisa was just owned by a super-wealthy person and it wasn’t on display and people couldn’t see it, couldn’t enjoy it.” He said at the time he hoped such a sale wouldn’t become a trend, adding that it could adversely affect scientific research and public education. Responding to Tuesday’s auction, Brusatte called it “harrowing” that Jodi could disappear from public view. “We’ve really just found out that Nanotyrannus is real, and now one of the best skeletons is about to be sold to the highest bidder, and it’s harrowing to think it could disappear into the vaults of a collector rather than displayed in a museum where it can wow and inspire kids and families and the public at large,” he told the BBC. But Jacobs told the Today programme on Tuesday that the debate had two sides, and that a lot of time, effort, and money went into excavating the specimens. “I don’t begrudge the people involved for wanting to sell it for such a large amount of money,” she said. “Although it’s a scary prospect, actually a lot of them have ended up in the public eye… these things without a doubt will end up in a museum at some point.”

items.title: Ballon d’Or africain : Pape Gueye assume ses ambitions
items.description: Dans un entretien accordé à Canal+ Sport Afrique, dans l’émission « Talents d’Afrique » du lundi 26 octobre 2026, le milieu de terrain sénégalais Pape Gueye revient sur son épanouissement à Villarreal, sa mise en retrait temporaire de la sélection après le Mondial et son ambition de remporter le Ballon d’Or africain. Pape Gueye affiche ses ambitions. Après une saison marquée par la victoire du Sénégal à la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN), au cours de laquelle il a inscrit le but décisif en finale, le milieu de terrain de Villarreal assume sa candidature au Ballon d’Or africain. Dans un entretien exclusif accordé à Canal+ Sport Afrique, le joueur sénégalais revient également sur son parcours récent et son attachement à l’équipe nationale. En Espagne, l’international sénégalais dit avoir trouvé un environnement favorable à son épanouissement. Après trois années passées à Villarreal, il assure se sentir bien au sein du club, où il bénéficie de la confiance de ses dirigeants et de bonnes conditions de travail. Sollicité par d’autres équipes lors du dernier mercato estival, il a choisi de poursuivre son aventure avec le club espagnol. « J’ai retrouvé mon meilleur niveau ici », explique-t-il, convaincu d’évoluer dans une équipe ambitieuse, capable de jouer les premières places et de se mesurer aux grandes formations européennes. Son objectif est de poursuivre sa progression et de contribuer aux ambitions de Villarreal. La CAN remportée avec le Sénégal a également marqué un tournant dans sa carrière. Le milieu de terrain estime que son but en finale a changé le regard porté sur lui, aussi bien au Sénégal qu’en Europe. Il raconte notamment avoir reçu les félicitations de joueurs du Real Madrid après cette rencontre, preuve, selon lui, de l’écho suscité par cette finale. « J’ai réagi sous le coup de l’émotion » L’entretien a également été l’occasion pour Pape Gueye de revenir sur sa décision de se mettre en retrait de la sélection nationale à l’issue de la Coupe du monde. Le joueur explique avoir beaucoup investi dans sa préparation pour cette compétition, avec l’ambition d’être au meilleur de sa forme pour servir son pays. Il évoque notamment les difficultés rencontrées dans la préparation, des tensions internes et sa frustration après avoir été remplacé assez tôt lors du match contre la Belgique, suivi de la défaite sénégalaise. « Je suis humain, c’était la goutte de trop et j’ai réagi sous le coup de l’émotion », reconnaît-il. Le milieu de terrain affirme toutefois avoir tourné cette page. Avec le recul, il considère cet épisode comme une expérience qui lui a permis de grandir. Il entend désormais regarder vers l’avenir et contribuer à écrire de nouvelles pages de l’histoire du football sénégalais. Pape Gueye insiste aussi sur la nécessité d’accompagner la nouvelle génération, qu’il juge particulièrement talentueuse. Il souligne l’importance de l’encadrement et des conseils du nouveau sélectionneur, dont il apprécie notamment l’expérience à son poste de milieu de terrain. Pour le joueur de Villarreal, l’objectif collectif reste clair : rendre fiers les Sénégalais et tout mettre en œuvre pour remporter la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des nations. Un Ballon d’Or africain dans le viseur Sur le plan individuel, Pape Gueye ne cache pas son ambition. Après une saison au cours de laquelle il affirme avoir atteint plusieurs objectifs, notamment sur le plan collectif, il considère légitime de figurer parmi les candidats au Ballon d’Or africain. « Au début de saison, je note toujours mes objectifs de buts, de passes décisives, de matchs joués, de trophées collectifs et individuels, et le Ballon d’Or africain faisait partie de mes objectifs », confie-t-il, tout en rappelant que le choix appartient aux votants. Le Sénégalais évoque également les deux compatriotes qui ont déjà remporté cette distinction, El-Hadji Diouf et Sadio Mané, qu’il considère comme des légendes du football national. Remporter à son tour ce trophée représenterait, selon lui, une immense fierté et l’aboutissement d’un parcours marqué par des moments difficiles. En attendant le verdict, Pape Gueye entend poursuivre sa progression en club et rester mobilisé pour la sélection. Entre ambitions individuelles et objectifs collectifs, le milieu sénégalais affiche sa volonté de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa carrière. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE

items.title: Brahim Ghali contesté de l’intérieur, le polisario se déchire
items.description: Un enregistrement attribué à Bachir Mustapha Sayed, frère du fondateur du « polisario » et président de son « Conseil national », met à nu les fractures au sommet du mouvement séparatiste, à l’approche de la nouvelle résolution du Conseil de sécurité relative au Sahara marocain. Un enregistrement qui circule, attribué au dénommé Bachir Mustapha Sayed, frère du fondateur du front séparatiste « polisario » et président de son soi-disant « Conseil national », dévoile l’ampleur des fissures et la lutte acharnée pour le pouvoir dans les camps de Tindouf. Il y fustige Brahim Ghali, l’actuel chef du front, et se dit prêt à briguer la direction du mouvement. Cette passe d’armes intervient à l’approche de la décision attendue du Conseil de sécurité sur la question du Sahara marocain, alors que circule un projet de texte qui met fin aux rêves de sécession et consacre la proposition marocaine d’autonomie comme seule et unique solution pour régler ce différend. Les critiques de ce dirigeant séparatiste et l’aveu de son ambition d’évincer Ghali pour lui succéder dépassent le simple désaccord passager. Elles traduisent une secousse violente au cœur de l’organisation séparatiste soutenue par l’Algérie, dont la direction actuelle a perdu sa boussole ainsi que sa légitimité politique et organisationnelle. Faute du moindre progrès sur le terrain comme sur le plan diplomatique, son projet séparatiste vacille sous le poids des querelles de leadership et de postes. Dans ce contexte, une source bien informée des affaires des camps, ancien cadre du « polisario », affirme que « la décision attendue du Conseil de sécurité, si elle est adoptée conformément au projet américain et dans la version présentée, posera un défi majeur au polisario, d’autant qu’elle fermera définitivement la porte à l’option de l’autodétermination et limitera la négociation à la seule solution d’autonomie ». Cette même source ajoute que « cette évolution placera le “polisario” tout entier devant une impasse majeure : dès la publication de la décision, un débat profond et décisif s’ouvrira dans les camps sur leur avenir et celui de l’organisation dans son ensemble, d’autant que le projet américain touche à tous les volets du dossier, en imposant notamment le recensement de la population des camps. Cela fait de cette décision un tournant radical dans le cours du conflit, qui oblige le front à une révision complète de ses choix ». L’ancien cadre du « polisario » explique que « l’adoption de la décision dans la version ayant fuité, ou dans une version proche, placera le “polisario” à la croisée des chemins et l’obligera à opérer des changements radicaux dans son parcours, ses dirigeants et ses orientations politiques, maintenant que les contours de l’avenir sont tracés. À défaut, il se verrait contraint de restructurer ses rangs et d’entrer dans une confrontation ouverte, un bras de fer déclaré avec la communauté internationale et les États-Unis d’Amérique, une option qui comporte un coût exorbitant ». La source au fait des affaires des camps poursuit : « Les dirigeants du front, à tous les niveaux, perdront leur influence réelle si la décision est entérinée dans sa forme actuelle, car il ne restera plus à l’organisation de marge d’action. Cela signifie que le projet séparatiste, dans sa configuration présente, est arrivé à son terme et condamné de fait à mort, ce qui laisse présager une révolte interne prochaine et des changements profonds et inéluctables dans les camps ». Elle souligne que « le sort final du dossier dépendra avant tout de l’Algérie. Si la décision est adoptée dans sa version américaine actuelle, l’attention internationale se portera sur la position algérienne plutôt que sur celle du “polisario”, qui deviendra peu à peu un fardeau et un problème algérien interne, alors qu’elle était une question régionale ». La même source relève que « la prochaine décision, conformément aux orientations du projet américain, exonère le Maroc de toute exigence internationale et adresse directement les obligations internationales au “polisario et à l’Algérie” : cessez-le-feu, règlement de la question des réfugiés, engagement plein et entier dans la légalité internationale, circonscrite à l’initiative d’autonomie. Les regards se tournent dès lors vers la réponse officielle qu’Alger adoptera après la décision, afin de dessiner les contours de la période à venir, car le “polisario” n’a plus d’atouts à faire valoir dans une négociation, et l’Algérie n’a pas encore dévoilé sa position définitive ». The post Brahim Ghali contesté de l’intérieur, le polisario se déchire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: We’re not behind waving of Russian flags during 2024 protests in Nigeria – Russia Foreign Minister
items.description: Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov has dismissed insinuations that the Russian government sponsored some Nigerian youths who waved Russian flags during the 2024 #EndBadGovernance protests. Lavrov, who spoke in Moscow on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit, in response to a question by the News Agency of Nigeria, said Russia had no hand in the action and distanced Moscow from any attempt to undermine Nigeria’s sovereignty. According to him, Russia and Nigeria enjoy a robust relationship dating back to the Soviet Union. He said those who wore Russian flags did so in their personal capacity and that it did not translate into official support from Russia. “Anyone, who donned the Russian flag, did so in his or her personal capacity. It does not mean that Russia was in support of this kind of action. “A lot of citizens sympathetic to Palestinians wave Palestinian flags to express solidarity. It does not mean the Palestinian government is behind them,” Lavrov said. The News Agency of Nigeria(NAN), recalls that the nationwide #EndBadGovernance protests took place from Aug. 1 to Aug. 10, 2024, with the protesters citing high cost of living and economic hardship for their action. NAN also recalls that during the protests, some groups of protesters, mostly youths and minors in Kano, Kaduna, Zamfara and Abuja, were seen waving Russian flags and chanting slogans calling for military intervention. The action, which the Federal Government described as treasonable and a threat to Nigeria’s sovereignty, led to the arrest of scores of protesters and some tailors who were allegedly sewing the flags. The Russian Embassy in Abuja had, at the time, also denied any involvement. Lavrov said the robust relationship between Nigeria and Russia had seen an increase in scholarships awarded to Nigerians, reaching a peak of 220 in 2026. He recalled that in 2024, he met with his Nigerian counterpart in Abuja who warmly received him, and cemented the bilateral ties between the two countries. On defence pacts with some countries in the Sahel, Lavrov said Russia was helping to eliminate security threats in the region, adding that Moscow was aware that some Western capitals were using Ukrainian mercenaries to sabotage the efforts, as they did in Libya, in a bid to undermine regional stability. Commenting on the recent diesel supply agreement with the United States, the foreign minister said it was purely a business decision and would not affect the interest of its allies. “The diesel agreement with the U.S. is purely a business decision by two world leaders who are concerned by the rising cost of energy,” he said. items.title: Mbappé sorry for ‘ill-judged’ Mao remark after backlash in China
items.description: Kylian Mbappé has apologised for “ill-judged” comments about late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which led several Chinese brands to drop him. Mbappé reportedly told the French talk show The Bridge about the meme “that makes me laugh the most, it’s the one where there’s a video of a guy, I think it’s a Chinese dictator…” He then laughs as the clip cuts to a meme showing his face superimposed on an image resembling Mao. The meme is part of a running joke about the Real Madrid forward being called a “dictator” because of his huge influence in football. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world,” Mbappé said in a statement. “I apologise to everyone my words have upset.” Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappé’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans”. The joke did not go down well in China, where Mao is revered by the Communist Party, despite his chaotic and often violent rule that left millions dead. A few people came out in his support on Chinese social media, but that’s rare given China’s tightly controlled internet, where people are expected to toe the party and government line on sensitive topics. Few topics are as sensitive as Mao, which may explain why brands were so quick to terminate partnerships with a global sports star like Mbappé. The show’s YouTube channel doesn’t have the original video, and it’s unclear when the interview, hosted by Real Madrid’s Aurélien Tchouaméni, first aired. In clips circulating online, Mbappé does not name Mao. He says he “uses [the meme] with friends all the time”. The furore appeared to kick off Monday night after Chinese football forum Dongqiudi drew attention to the comments in a statement, calling them “inappropriate” and saying they “hurt the feelings of Chinese people”. Screengrabs of the clip and meme have since spread quickly on Chinese social media, with people echoing this sentiment and even calling for a boycott of both the French striker and his club, Real Madrid. But some have blurred the meme itself as well as the part of the comment they found offensive, when Mbappe refers to “a Chinese dictator”. Dongqiudi said in its statement that it was “unable to translate” his comments because they were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. Many people are therefore also wondering what exactly Mbappe said and have responded to the angry posts and comments with questions, wanting to know more. Weibo users are recirculating the clip by blurring the meme and redacting references to Mao What is the reaction in China? Chinese fans have been criticising Mbappé – who is popular in China and has huge brand endorsements – of “profiting from the Chinese market yet making remarks that offend the Chinese public”. “International public figures, in particular, should show greater respect and sensitivity, as national sentiment must never be taken lightly,” reads another comment on Weibo. As online anger grew louder, Chinese brands began cutting ties, though they did not explicitly refer to the video. The country’s largest dairy producer, Mengniu, said it “firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people”. Drinks giant Dongpeng issued a similar statement: “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments.” According to state-owned newspaper The Global Times, state broadcaster CCTV’s news apps will not feature content related to the French striker. Chinese media reported on Tuesday that CCTV will also stop showing La Liga matches. Real Madrid is one of 20 clubs in the Spanish football league and is the most decorated team, with 36 league titles. China’s foreign ministry has also weighed in, with spokesperson Lin Jian saying: “We have noted the relevant reports. Words and deeds that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with opposition from all sectors of Chinese society.” Mbappé has a significant commercial presence in China China is a major market for international sports stars and homegrown brands have signed multimillion-dollar endorsement contracts with Mbappé, Norwegian striker Erling Haaland, and NBA player Stephen Curry. By 14:00 local time on Tuesday, five of the top 10 trending topics on Weibo centred on Mbappé, with the hashtag “multiple brands terminate partnerships with Mbappé” topping the list. “Don’t ever come to China,” read one of Weibo’s top comments. Why is Mao a sensitive topic? Mao founded the People’s Republic of China in 1949 and ruled through the tumultuous 1960s and 1970s. His attempt at rapid industrialisation, the Great Leap Forward, led to a famine that killed tens of millions. Then came the Cultural Revolution: a violent purge of anyone seen as a threat to Communism, which included Chinese intellectuals, landowners, artists and often rivals within the Party. His death in 1976 ushered in a new era for China, as it began to open its doors to the global economy. Even as the country moved away from Mao’s rule, the party continued to hail him as a national icon whose legacy was beyond reproach. So jokes or memes about Mao are seen not just as an insult to the party but also to its closely guarded narrative about the country’s past. Mbappé has said some of the memes “reveal a lack of political and human awareness” It’s unclear when the Mbappé meme involving Mao began, but his nickname, “the dictator”, has made the striker the subject of many memes and jokes online. Mbappé is widely regarded as one of the world’s best footballers and has wielded significant influence at the clubs he has played for. His extraordinary speed, goalscoring ability, and worldwide popularity have made him a global icon, attracting millions of fans, major sponsorship deals, and media attention, with his influence extending into fashion, culture, and business. In 2024, he sued a French influencer and kebab shop owner for using his name in the description of one of the shop’s sandwiches, leading to more jokes about the nickname. France teammate Ousmane Dembele jumped on the trend during the 2026 World Cup, calling Mbappé Mobut – a reference to Mobutu Sese Seko, the dictator who ruled the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire, for three decades. In a September interview with France Football, Mbappé acknowledged the light-heartedness behind many of these memes, but said they “sometimes reveal a lack of political and human awareness among people”. “There’s a side that’s a bit less funny, because we know the damage people like that have caused throughout history,” he said. “Being compared to people who murder others, or who have made millions upon millions of people miserable… I don’t think I’ve done that in my life.”

items.title: South Africa evacuation expenditure ‘smacks of a grand scheme of corruption’ – Abu Jinapor
items.description: The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, has accused the Foreign Affairs Ministry of failing to adequately account for expenditure on the evacuation of Ghanaians from South Africa, describing the entire exercise as a “grand scheme of corruption to siphon public funds”. According to him, the discrepancies surrounding the GH¢49.72 million evacuation expenditure raise serious concerns about possible misappropriation of public funds, fraud and corruption, warranting an independent investigation into the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Jinapor said the Minority believes GH¢16.4 million remains unaccounted for and has renewed its demand for Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to resign pending an independent audit. “The point is that the totality of this whole South Africa evacuation accounted in expenditure smacks of a grand scheme of corruption to siphon public funds and in that case the minister should take ultimate responsibility,” he said. Mr Jinapor said the concerns go beyond questions about whether the expenditure was adequately documented, pointing to alleged duplicate entries, discrepancies in payment records and cases where individuals reportedly signed for allowances they did not receive in full or at all. Read also: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments He also cited expenditure records without supporting receipts and questions surrounding the chartered flights used during the evacuation. “We have consistently maintained that some 16.4 million Ghana cedis is unaccounted for,” he said. According to him, the Minority’s concerns have been reinforced by the Multimedia Group’s JoyNews Research documentary aired on Monday, October 26, which examined discrepancies in documents provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Research investigation reported apparent discrepancies in payment records, including questionable signatures, as part of its examination of how the GH¢49.72 million expenditure was accounted for. Mr Jinapor further questioned why documents subsequently provided to Joy FM differed from those supplied to the Minority and Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee following a request under the Right to Information Act, 2019 (Act 989). He alleged that some of the documents appeared to have been prepared to address gaps in the Ministry’s account of the exercise. “Subsequent to that, Joy FM was given documentation which was not within the contours of the documents which were provided to the Minority, which was provided to the Foreign Affairs Committee,” he said. “And these documents, even when examined, it’s established clearly that these documents were conjured to kind of plug holes into the whole case which has been established.” He argued that the differences in the records, alongside the other alleged irregularities, made an independent investigation necessary to establish how the public funds were spent. The Minority is therefore calling for an investigation by an independent, internationally reputable auditing and accounting firm. Mr Jinapor said the Foreign Affairs Minister should step aside while the investigation is conducted, arguing that his continued stay in office could undermine confidence in the process. The Minority’s demands follow the controversy over the GH¢49,721,786 reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa between May 27 and September 4, 2026, amid renewed xenophobic attacks. The expenditure, according to figures presented by Mr Ablakwa, comprised GH¢38.84 million for chartered flights, commercial tickets, ground transportation, feeding, accommodation and medical care; GH¢10.8 million for reintegration and transport allowances; and GH¢84,274 for repatriating the remains of two Ghanaian nationals and related autopsy costs. Read also: VIDEO: Ablakwa details GH¢49.7m SA evacuation spending, rejects Minority’s claims of unaccounted funds The Minister has rejected the Minority’s allegations, insisting that all the funds have been accounted for. He has also requested an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken by successive governments since 2017. The disputed expenditure and supporting documentation remain subject to further scrutiny, with the Minority insisting that an independent audit is necessary to establish whether any public funds were misappropriated.

items.title: Flying Across the World to Vote
items.description: Photographs and Videos by Dana Golan Since the beginning of the Gaza war, a record number of Israelis have left the country. More than 10 percent of the electorate now lives abroad, and the country generally does not allow absentee ballots: Those who want to vote in today’s election, the first since October 7, need to be there in person. An estimated 67,000 Israeli expats have traveled thousands of miles—and spent thousands of dollars—to return home. Within Israel, the polls suggest a fairly even split between the parties that favor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and those that oppose him. But most of the expats are expected to support the opposition. The prime minister’s allies reportedly considered restricting airport capacity to limit the number of arrivals. But the flights still came. Israelis returning from abroad expressed feelings of deep investment in this election and a belief that the outcome will affect them no matter where they live. Many are willing to travel a long way to vote for what they believe will be a better future. Dana Golan for The Atlantic Maya Mor Mitrani, a college student and opera singer in Philadelphia, spoke of concern for her father, who has served in the military reserves since October 7. “I just think the situation is really bad,” she said, “and I want to have at least some influence over how the government tries to solve the problems we’re facing right now. So if my influence amounts to just one ballot in the box, that’s what I’ll do.” Dana Golan for The Atlantic Jonathan Matkowsky was born in America, but he moved to Israel in 2012. On October 7, he barricaded his children indoors and drove south to help however he could, working as a volunteer driver for off-duty soldiers and civilians for the next four months. He later moved back to the United States. Now he has returned for the election: “It’s a meaningful vote for me because of how much trauma we’ve been through,” he said. Although he considered voting for Gadi Eisenkot because of his support for extending the draft to the ultra-Orthodox, he ultimately decided to vote for Netanyahu. He trusts the prime minister’s wisdom and experience and credits him with keeping Israel safe: “I’m proud of him. I believe in him. I think he’s a hero,” he said. Dana Golan for The Atlantic New York’s John F. Kennedy airport on Oct 25th, 2026. Dana Golan for The Atlantic Dana Golan for The Atlantic An organization called Fly&Vote organized expats to fly from New York to Tel Aviv on October 25th. Dana Golan for The Atlantic Shirily Bar-Or spent years protesting in Israel before moving to Athens last year. “I didn’t give up, exactly. I just needed to breathe. I was running out of air. I hope I’ll be able to breathe again tomorrow.” What she wants, she said, is for “the country to be sane again. I want a government that works for the public good. I want democracy.” To her this election is pivotal because, she said, what Netanyahu wants “is to destroy us just to save his own skin.” Dana Golan for The Atlantic Dan Galezer lives in New York and already had a trip to Israel planned, but he changed his flight to be there on Election Day. He said that he didn’t know which opposition party to support, but that “I’m just at the stage of saying: Get Bibi out of the seat already. His time is up.” Galezer’s family’s kibbutz was the site of one of the worst massacres on October 7. “Today, even after everything that’s happened,” he said, “I don’t rule out returning.” But whether that will even be possible, he said, may depend on the outcome of the election: “This feels like a breaking point.” Dana Golan for The Atlantic Arie Deizer has lived in Bucharest for 30 years and compared Netanyahu to the Hungarian strongman Viktor Orbán. Netanyahu, he said, has “destroyed the country—he’s completely lost it now,” and Deizer hopes he’ll be “thrown out, just like Orbán.” Deizer is voting for the Democrats, in part because unlike many other opposition parties, they have not ruled out working with Arab parties should they win. “I hope we’ll have an overwhelming majority here—70 seats—so that the Arab parties can’t be ignored.” Dana Golan for The Atlantic A sign on the entrance to a shop in Jaffa, Tel Aviv, reads, "Jews and Arabs refuse to be enemies." Dana Golan for The Atlantic Shai Sinai hasn’t lived in Israel for 40 years, but he’s come back from Hamburg to vote in every election since Netanyahu came to power. “I was born here, I grew up here, I was educated here, I served in the army here, and my whole family—the family members who are still alive—basically lives here.” Volunteers from Fly&Vote, a nonprofit dedicated to helping expats return for the election, met him and other voters at the airport. So did members of the Democrats, a party Sinai said he will support. He hopes that the government will be replaced, he said, but “to say that I’m expecting it would be too optimistic.” Dana Golan for The Atlantic Volunteers and candidates from The Democrats party came to greet Israelis as they landed in Israel to vote. Dana Golan for The Atlantic Election posters at the entrance to a polling station in Tel Aviv include one from Naftali Bennett's 'B'Yachad' party that reads, "Together We Will Fix."

items.title: Ex-wife of Zimbabwe’s vice-president freed after collapse of attempted murder case
items.description: The former wife of Zimbabwe’s vice-president has been freed from remand after seven years while on trial for his attempted murder. Marry Mubaiwa was charged in 2019, after her then husband Gen Constantino Chiwenga accused her of trying to impede his medical treatment in South Africa. Ordering her release, a magistrate said Mubaiwa had suffered mental, physical and financial prejudice during the trial, state-owned daily the Herald said. The ruling was made after the state asked for the trial to be postponed by a month in order to engage witnesses. Her lawyer described the ruling as a victory that had come too late, because her client’s rights had been violated by the delay in the trial. Speaking outside court in the capital Harare on Tuesday, the lawyer added that if the state moved for a new trial, they would deal with it when it happened. Mubaiwa was accused of attempting to kill Chiwenga, while he was in hospital in Pretoria. The vice-president then went to China for four months of treatment. Mubaiwa was remanded in custody and denied bail. According to the New Zimbabwe news website, Mubaiwa celebrated her release outside court, and said justice had been achieved and that she was proud of her lawyer. In 2017, Chiwenga played a key role in overthrowing then President Robert Mugabe.

items.title: ‎Investigator defends methods in Tano Nnimire mining trial
items.description: A police investigator has told an Accra High Court that he inherited an incomplete docket in the alleged illegal mining case involving Bernard Antwi Boasiako and Akonta Mining Company Limited.‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Akpo Glover said he studied the docket before continuing the investigations and did not alter any part of the inherited records.‎ ‎ ‎He was testifying under cross-examination in the ongoing trial of Boasiako, a former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), and Akonta Mining Company Limited. ‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Glover, who has 17 years of policing experience, rejected the suggestion that his understanding of the case was based on “second-hand information”.‎ ‎ ‎”My understanding of this case is as a result of various methods of investigation the police conducted. They include interviews with witnesses, visits to crime scenes, drone surveillance and review of documents,” he said. ‎ ‎ ‎The investigator said two prosecution witnesses had stated in their caution statements that Akonta Mining erected barriers and side poles in the Tano Nnimire Forest to prevent people, including Forestry Commission officials, from entering the reserve.‎ ‎ ‎He said his investigations implicated Boasiako and Akonta Mining in the alleged illegal mining activities.‎ ‎ ‎Detective Chief Inspector Glover also disputed a suggestion by defence counsel, Mr Samuel Atta Akyea, that letters written to the Western Regional Security Council over alleged illegal mining on Boasiako’s concession demonstrated opposition to illegal mining by those involved.‎ ‎ ‎He maintained that agents of Boasiako and Akonta Mining had acted in their own interests in the Tano Nnimire Forest.‎‎ ‎ ‎The investigator recalled that the letter to the Western Regional Security Council was dated June 2021.‎ ‎ ‎The court adjourned the case to October 27, 2026.‎ ‎Boasiako and Akonta Mining face charges over alleged mining operations without a licence in the Tano Nnimire Forest Reserve in the Western Region.‎ ‎ ‎The prosecution alleged that the accused persons felled about 300 merchantable trees in the reserve and erected structures without written permission from the Forestry Commission.‎ ‎ ‎Boasiako, a 50-year-old entrepreneur, has denied the charges. ‎He is serving a 20-year prison sentence for a similar offence. ‎

items.title: Importations agricoles : l’Algérie fixe un délai pour le dépôt du PPI 2027
items.description: Le ministère de l’Agriculture a fixé un délai aux importateurs de bovins sur pieds, de lait, de produits laitiers et d’intrants avicoles pour déposer leurs programmes prévisionnels d’importation (PPI) pour l’année 2027. Ces opérateurs ont jusqu’au 31 octobre pour effectuer cette formalité indispensable pour obtenir les licences d’importation et entamer les démarches bancaires pour la domiciliation de leurs opérations. Ce délai a été fixé le 7 octobre dernier. « Il est porté à la connaissance des opérateurs économiques concernés par les opérations d'importation de bovins sur pieds, intrants avicoles, lait et produits laitiers, relevant du contrôle sanitaire vétérinaire, que le dépôt des programmes prévisionnels d'importation (PPI) au titre de l'année 2027 devra être effectué au plus tard le 31 octobre 2026 », a indiqué la direction générale des services vétérinaires de ce ministère. PPI : le ministère de l’Agriculture veut un respect strict des délais Cette dernière a demandé dans la même note aux importateurs de ces produits de « veiller à renseigner avec précision la nature des produits et les quantités prévisionnelles prévues pour la période ». Il est également exigé des opérateurs concernés de respecter « strictement les délais fixés afin de permettre d'assurer le traitement des programmes. » Le département de Sidi Ali Khaldi prend ainsi les devants afin d’éviter d’éventuelles perturbations dans l’approvisionnement du marché en ces produits essentiels pour la production des viandes et la disponibilité du lait et des produits laitiers sur le marché national. Le PPI a été instauré en juillet 2025 pour réguler et renforcer le contrôle sur les importations. Depuis, toute opération d’importation doit être précédée obligatoirement de la validation du PPI par le ministère du Commerce extérieur et de la Promotion des exportations. L’article Importations agricoles : l’Algérie fixe un délai pour le dépôt du PPI 2027 est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The Greatest to Blade Runner 2099: 12 of the best TV shows to watch this November
items.description: From a drama about Muhammad Ali’s early years to Amy Poehler’s latest sitcom and a Blade Runner small-screen spin-off – these are the best series to watch and stream. 1. The Gilded Age The fourth season of Julian Fellowes’ addictive period drama picks up soon after the previous season ended and answers some burning, melodramatic questions. Will the nouveau riche George Russell (Morgan Spector), having moved out of their ostentatious mansion, go home to his manipulative social-climbing wife, Bertha (Carrie Coon)? Will the pedigreed Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) topple Bertha from the top of the social ladder? She’s certainly going to try. Subplots swirl around them as Peggy (Denée Benton) tries to maintain her career as a writer while dealing with her intrusive mother-in-law-to-be (Phylicia Rashad), while Marian (Louisa Jacobson) and Larry’s (Harry Richardson) on-and-off romance gets especially thorny. Last season’s ratings were among the show’s highest, so there may even be an appetite for the upcoming Voices of the Gilded Age: The Christmas Album , featuring songs from the Broadway-veteran cast. If you’ve ever wanted to hear Baranski sing We Need a Little Christmas or Brian Stokes Mitchell do It’s the Most Wonderful Time of the Year, here you go. The Gilded Age premieres 1 November on HBO in the US and 2 November on Sky Atlantic in the UK 2. The Greatest Muhammad Ali was one of the greatest boxers of all time and has also been one of the most often depicted on screen, from Will Smith in the 2001 film Ali to documentaries by Antoine Fuqua and Ken Burns. This dramatic series sets itself apart by focusing on his childhood and the early years of his career, when he was still known as Cassius Clay, in a story that moves from his boyhood in the Jim Crow South to the 1960 Olympics, through to the 1964 fight that made him the world champion. Newcomer Jaalen Best plays Ali in the show, which has the cooperation of the Ali family and counts his widow, Lonnie Ali, and Michael B Jordan as executive producers. “The Greatest is [about] his pathway to growth, at home with his brother and his parents. It’s a granular deep dive into Muhammad’s life,” Lonnie Ali told Esquire . Meanwhile the series’ creator, Ben Watkins (showrunner of the Alex Cross series), teased that despite its family ties, the details on screen “aren’t always flattering”. The Greatest premieres 4 November on Prime Video internationally 3. Stick For some reason, middle-aged former golf champions trying to make a comeback are a mini-trend in sitcoms. Will Ferrell’s character set out to do it as the title character in the tongue-in-cheek Netflix series Hawk. And in the second season of Apple TV’s Stick, a comedy that leans toward the heartwarming, Owen Wilson’s character – Pryce Cahill, known as Stick – attempts to come out of retirement too. The cast has always been this show’s biggest draw, and that is enhanced this season with Rhea Seehorn of Pluribus and Better Call Saul in a supporting role as Stick’s new coach. Timothy Olyphant returns as his former rival, who nudges him to try to become the oldest player ever to win the US Open tournament, with Judy Greer as Stick’s ex-wife and Marc Maron as his friend and caddie, Mitts. Apparently the burgeoning television golf world requires cringe-making nicknames. Stick premieres 4 November on Apple TV internationally 4. Black Doves Keira Knightley and Ben Whishaw return in the second season of this thoroughly improbable but always entertaining action-espionage series. Knightley plays Helen Webb, whose husband (Andrew Buchan) is about to become the UK’s prime minister – a situation that is not great for him because she has been leaking information for a decade to the shadowy Black Doves organisation, set on undermining governments around the world. Whishaw plays her best friend, Sam, a hitman who helps her get out of the scrapes while getting into some himself. In the new season, Helen’s Black Doves handler, Mrs Reed, played by Sarah Lancashire, seems to go missing, although Lancashire herself remains a major part of the show. Marital drama plays out in the background of the shootouts and power plays. The new PM might not be fit to govern since he hasn’t noticed his wife spying right under his nose. Or maybe she’s just that clever. The series creator, Joe Barton, captured its droll tone when calling the characters “our murderous little spy family”. Black Doves premieres 5 November on Netflix internationally (Credit: Channel 4) 5. It Gets Worse Leo Reich, who broke through with his HBO stand-up comedy special Literally Who Cares? in 2023, created and stars in this acerbic series about three Gen Z university friends struggling through their early 20s, characters Reich has described as “self-involved and quite objectionable”. He plays the self-absorbed Ethan, supported by his parents. His best friends are by-the-rules Abi (Emily Fairn) and would-be writer Sam (Olivia Gray). It’s a sign of Reich’s rising star that he has enticed some big names to join in. Andrew Scott appears in an episode, Lena Dunham has a cameo as Abi’s boss and the series’ unlikely narrator is the novelist Zadie Smith. The show is not just another Friends knockoff. It was a hit at the recent London Film Festival, with the Financial Times calling it “a witty Gen Z sex comedy” and the Guardian describing the series as “profound and properly funny” and Reich as “the future of TV comedy”. It Gets Worse is currently on Channel 4 in the UK and premieres 6 November on Paramount+ in the US 6. Rivals It has been months since the first half of this scathingly funny show’s second season dropped, but finally we’re back in the fictional Cotswold county of Rutshire, beloved from Jilly Cooper’s bonkbuster novels. It’s a place where cheating, in business and relationships, is just a way of life for its mix of mischievous, mean-spirited and occasionally good-hearted characters. Tony Baddingham, the tycoon played with devilish glee by David Tennant, is more sinister than ever, and unlikely to soften in the aftermath of a tragedy. His rival, Declan O’Hara (Aidan Turner), is ever more desperate to keep his career and marriage intact, which his wife is making more difficult on both counts. And their daughter Taggie (Bella Maclean) must decide whether to give into her love for the playboy Rupert Campbell-Black (Alex Hassell) or do the sensible thing and run for the hills. In the new episodes, Lady Monica Baddingham’s glamorous younger sister turns up. So does a legendary Argentinian polo player. They should fit right in. Rivals premieres 11 November on Hulu in the US and Disney+ in the UK 7. The Good Daughter Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy – either one could be the good daughter in this thriller about murder, justice and family dynamics. They play sisters from the fictional smalltown of Pikeville, Georgia, who survived a violent home invasion when they were girls. Byrne is Samantha, a patent lawyer who moved to New York. Fahy is Charlotte, who stayed in town and became a defence lawyer like their father (Brendan Gleeson). The sisters have been estranged for a decade, but when Charlotte witnesses a murder that recalls the attack in their childhood, the tension and mysteries ramp up and Samantha is called home. The Good Daughter – not to be confused with those other recent suspense series The Better Sister and The Girlfriend – is written by Karin Slaughter, based on her 2017 bestselling novel, and explores the traumatic effects of violence. “We’re all exposed to trauma all the time,” Fahy told Vanity Fair , adding, “It’s really important to show people navigating their trauma and coming out on the other side.” The Good Daughter premieres 12 November on Peacock in the US and Sky Atlantic in the UK 8. 12 12 12 Two commanding, high-profile actors star in this heist series. Jamie Dornan plays Paul Galvin, a criminal who tries to leave his old life but is forced back in as part of an $800m (£599m) theft from a Zurich bank. Anthony Mackie is Jack Strickland, a disgraced FBI agent on his trail, whose character handily explains the series’ title in the trailer . “FBI principles of crime say a high asset robbery is 12 months in planning, 12 hours in execution. A bank robber who’s not caught within 12 days is not caught at all,” he says. The show mingles those three timelines as the cat-and-mouse game takes the men across Europe – with spectacular settings on dark streets, at sea and against snowy landscapes – en route to their inevitable face-to-face. 12 12 12 premieres 13 November on Apple TV internationally 9. Blue Lights This fourth season of the exhilarating police series set in Belfast keeps things fresh by returning to a much-loved character from the past. Mo McIntyre, whose mother, Tina, runs the family crime ring, finally goes on trial for orchestrating the attack that killed Gerry Cliff (Richard Dornan), devastating his police colleagues, in season one. That storyline becomes a touching opportunity to look back at Gerry’s romance with his wife, Sandra (beautifully played by Andi Osho), a sergeant who worked alongside him in Blackthorn Station. Apart from the trial, the team of regular characters grapples with anti-immigrant protests that turn violent. And all the while, higher-ups are threatening to shut down Blackthorn for inefficiency. As always, the show deftly puts crime-fighting against the backdrop of lingering political divisions going back to the Troubles, while mixing in personal stories. The Guardian , in its review of this season, rightly called it “TV’s most thrilling cop show”. Blue Lights is currently on BBC iPlayer in the UK and premieres 12 November on Britbox in the US 10. The Altruists Another day, another drama about a tech-adjacent mogul. This time it’s the saga of Sam Bankman-Fried, coming in the wake of those about Mark Zuckerberg ( The Social Reckoning ), Elizabeth Holmes ( You Can See Everything ) or Sam Altman ( Artificial ). Anthony Boyle ( House of Guinness ) plays Bankman-Fried, who founded the cryptocurrency exchange FTX, which fell apart in 2022. Convicted of fraud, conspiracy and money-laundering, he is currently in prison. (He is appealing his conviction and has formally requested a presidential pardon .) Julia Garner, who played a different fraudster in Inventing Anna , is Bankman-Fried’s colleague and sometime girlfriend, Caroline Ellison, who pleaded guilty to wire fraud. The series was created by Graham Moore, who won an Oscar for his screenplay of The Imitation Game, and who has an unusual, to say the least, take on the convicted criminals. In his view, Moore has said , Bankman-Fried and Ellison started as “deeply committed altruists,” out to change the financial world for everyone’s benefit, then “with the very best of intentions talked each other and themselves into committing a number of terrible crimes”. The Altruists premieres 19 November on Netflix internationally 11. Dig Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie play archaeologists on a dig in Greece, a setting Poehler has said is ideal for comedy. “A dig is a really funny place,” she told TV Insider . “It’s part summer camp, part mysterious uncovering of relics.” Laurie goes back to his wry comic roots as professor Neville Wycombe, who runs the archaeological program, and Poehler is Elise, the dedicated, serious head of a team of women. They arrive for the summer only to find themselves in an international muddle when they discover a priceless artifact. Geraldine Viswanathan and Antonia Thomas are members of Elise’s team, with Fina Strazza as Wycombe’s guileless in-over-her-head assistant. Poehler created the show with Mike Schur, a creator of her previous series, Parks and Recreation, one of television’s best sitcoms. Schur is a master of smart, low-key character-driven comedies including The Good Place, so whatever madcap adventures the archaeologists land in, the show promises to be slyly funny. Dig premieres 23 November on Peacock in the US 12. Blade Runner 2099 Michelle Yeoh stars in this series that takes the Blade Runner franchise racing toward everyone’s worst fears about artificial intelligence. In Ridley Scott’s classic film Blade Runner and Denis Villeneuve’s sequel, Blade Runner 2049, humans hunted down replicants. Now the robots have taken over and replicants are hunting down humans. Yeoh plays Olwen, a replicant on the Los Angeles police force. Hunter Schafer is Cora, who is actually a human masquerading as a replicant, so she can worm her way into the LA police as a way of protecting her brother. The series’ showrunner, Silka Luisa, told Empire magazine, “Everyone, globally, has been very aware of this palpable fear of the end of our species. Climate change, pandemics.” The series, she said, considers: “What would the world look like when it’s no longer ours?” Well, Cora is partnered with Olwen, who happens to be days from reaching the end of her lifespan, so while the world may be different, the old trope of an about-to-retire-cop paired with a rookie obviously lives on. Blade Runner 2099 premieres 25 November on Prime Video internationally

items.title: Gold Fields Health outreach screens 735 people, refers 21 suspected breast cancer cases
items.description: A health outreach programme organised by the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation and its partners has provided screening and general healthcare services to 735 people in Samahu and Abekoase in the Western Region, with 21 suspected breast cancer cases referred for further assessment. The fourth-quarter (Q4) Health Engagement and Access Link (HEAL) Programme, held on October 17, 2026, enabled 185 women to undergo breast cancer screening as part of activities marking Breast Cancer Awareness Month. It was organised under the theme “ Every Story is Unique, Every Journey Matters ” in partnership with the Rotary Club of Tarkwa, Unilever Ghana and Diagnostic Centre Limited (DCL). Speaking at the programme, Dr Magdalene D. Bakari, Lead Specialist for Health Services at Gold Fields Ghana Limited, stressed the importance of bringing healthcare closer to communities and encouraging people to seek medical attention early. She urged women to prioritise regular check-ups and seek professional advice whenever they notice unusual changes in their bodies. Beyond breast cancer screening, residents benefited from general medical consultations, blood pressure and blood sugar tests, eye and dental screenings, ear, nose and throat assessments, lung function tests, X-rays and ultrasound services. Free medication, health counselling and referrals for further care were also provided where necessary. The Executive Secretary of the Gold Fields Ghana Foundation, Abdel-Razak Yakubu, said the Foundation’s health outreach initiatives form part of efforts to improve access to essential healthcare in its host communities. The programme also provided National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) registration, renewal and card replacement services to 937 community members, helping them access health insurance services. With an estimated cost of GH¢606,964, the outreach reflects efforts by the Foundation and its partners to promote preventive healthcare, improve access to screening, and encourage the early detection of diseases.
