items.title: Assessing Ghana’s government policy on contract mining and local economic benefits
items.description: Pursuant to the passage of the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2431), the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has announced that indigenous Ghanaian companies are to undertake contract mining for surface mining operations, while underground contract mining should be conducted through partnerships in which Ghanaian-owned companies hold not less than 50 percent interest. For the purpose of clarification, contract mining refers to an arrangement in which a holder of a mineral right engages an independent corporate entity to execute mining operations, including drilling, blasting, excavation, haulage, equipment maintenance, dewatering, and rehabilitation. With this explanation, it is clear that the policy is a step in the right direction. However, for the successful implementation of this policy, the government must consider the myriad challenges that could hinder its implementation while identifying the potential benefits of this groundbreaking policy for Ghana’s mining sector. Contract mining would undoubtedly create opportunities for direct and indirect employment for many Ghanaians. Both skilled and unskilled members of the Ghanaian workforce would have roles to play in mining operations. Operators would be required to operate dump trucks, excavators, drill rigs, service trucks, and other equipment. Some of these positions do not require advanced academic qualifications, although the necessary training, licences, and practical competencies may be required. According to the Ghana Chamber of Mines, nearly 42 percent of employees in mining firms are indigenous people. This suggests that transferring mining operations to local contractors could create opportunities to increase employment among Ghanaians, thereby providing sustainable jobs for the country’s large population of unemployed youth. A Ghanaian-owned company conducting mining operations for a mining company can help retain a greater share of mining-related expenditure within the local economy, in both cedis and foreign currency. The contractor pays its workers from the revenue it earns, purchases locally available spare parts, and engages Ghanaian transport companies to transport its workers and materials. These activities promote the circulation of money within the economy while supporting other businesses. Where local contractors replace foreign service providers, some payments that would otherwise leave the country could be retained in Ghana. This could contribute to reducing foreign-exchange outflows and easing pressure on the cedi, particularly where local businesses also replace imported goods and services. However, the extent of these benefits would depend on the contractors’ reliance on imported equipment, spare parts, fuel, and other inputs. Another potential benefit is an increase in government tax revenue. According to the Minerals Commission, there are sixteen large-scale mining companies in the country. If indigenous Ghanaian companies undertake a greater share of the mining operations currently performed by foreign contractors, government revenue could increase through corporate income tax, PAYE income tax from workers, and other applicable taxes, including withholding tax on contract payments. The resulting revenue could support the government’s efforts to finance development projects across the country. Contract mining also presents an opportunity to develop Ghanaian-owned businesses. A Ghanaian entrepreneur could establish a company specialising in haulage, drilling, blasting, equipment maintenance, or other mining-related services. Existing indigenous mining companies could also take advantage of this policy to expand their businesses, strengthen their operational capacity, and improve their competitiveness in securing mining contracts. In assessing this policy holistically, it is important to consider the challenges that indigenous Ghanaian companies may face in undertaking mining operations. One of the major challenges is access to substantial capital. Surface mining operations, in particular, are equipment-intensive and require considerable investment in the acquisition of dump trucks, excavators, bulldozers, drill rigs, and other machinery. When a mining company transfers its load-and-haul operations to a contractor, the contractor is expected to provide a fleet of equipment capable of hauling ore and waste materials every day. Indigenous companies may struggle to obtain the necessary funding. Therefore, there should be appropriate financing arrangements between financial institutions and contractors. These arrangements should be developed after a thorough cost-benefit analysis and an assessment of the project’s financial viability by qualified engineers and financial experts. The introduction of contract mining should also create opportunities for public-private partnerships involving Ghanaian businesses to establish companies that provide mining-related goods and services. Page 47 of the Ghana Chamber of Mines’ 2024 report details expenditure of approximately US$240.7 million on imported consumables, including drill rods, drill bits, drill pipes, blasting consumables, and mobile equipment consumables such as tyres. Establishing local companies to manufacture or supply some of these goods could help retain a greater proportion of this expenditure within the Ghanaian economy and reduce the country’s dependence on imported mining inputs. The transfer of mining operations to indigenous Ghanaian companies could also raise concerns about workers’ wages, job security, allowances, and other employment benefits. Workers who previously worked directly for mining companies may experience changes in their conditions of service following the transfer of operations to contractors. Differences in salaries, allowances, and medical coverage could generate dissatisfaction among workers. Such grievances could lead to labour disputes, reduced morale, and the loss of experienced workers, thereby affecting the productivity of mining operations. The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, in conjunction with the Minerals Commission, should therefore be commended for recognising the importance of addressing these concerns. However, there must be effective enforcement of fair wage and allowance standards for contract mine workers. Workers should receive fair and transparent remuneration that takes into account their skills, experience and job responsibilities. Particular attention should be given to basic salaries, overtime payments, night-shift allowances, and adequate healthcare benefits for contract workers. In conclusion, Ghana’s contract mining policy presents a significant opportunity to transform the country’s mining sector into a stronger engine of local economic development. By empowering indigenous Ghanaian companies to undertake mining operations, the policy has the potential to create sustainable employment, promote local entrepreneurship, retain more value within the domestic economy, reduce dependence on imported mining inputs, and increase government revenue. However, the realisation of these benefits will depend on the government’s ability to address the financial, technical, operational, and labour-related challenges that may confront indigenous contractors. Ultimately, the success of contract mining should not be measured solely by the number of Ghanaian companies awarded mining contracts but by the extent to which the policy builds competitive Ghanaian businesses, creates decent jobs, strengthens local industries and improves the economic well-being of Ghanaians. ********* Author: Agyarko Ebenezer (Principal Mining Consultant and Head of Technical Communications, West Africa Cooperatives Networks [WACoN] )

items.title: SOCO projects to resume across northern Ghana, Oti Region, after funding delays resolved
items.description: The National Project Coordinator of the Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion (SOCO) Project, Elizabeth Ohenewa Agyei, has announced that stalled development projects across northern Ghana and the Oti Region are expected to resume following the resolution of funding delays. She said the World Bank-supported initiative had experienced a temporary disruption in the flow of funds, but the situation had since been addressed, with the Ministry of Finance releasing funds to facilitate the completion of ongoing projects. Speaking at a Ghana–Togo Joint Regional Working Session in Nalerigu in the North East Region on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, Ms Agyei said contractors were already mobilising to return to project sites. “Initially, there was a brief stall in the fund flow, but currently, that has been resolved. So, what we should expect is the pick-up of stalled projects that had to wait a while. I think that they have already started mobilising and coming back to site,” she said. She added that the Ministry of Finance was releasing most of the funding required to ensure the projects were completed. “Currently, we do not have that issue. We have the Minister of Finance actually releasing most of the funding that is required, especially to make sure that these projects are completed,” she stated. Ms Agyei also disclosed that discussions were ongoing about a possible third cycle of the project, expressing optimism about its prospects. “We are also in talks to get to know if we will do the third cycle, which we have high assurances of,” she added. The announcement offers renewed hope to communities across the beneficiary regions, where SOCO interventions aim to improve access to essential infrastructure, strengthen livelihoods and address development challenges that could contribute to social tensions. The working session brought together stakeholders from Ghana and Togo to review project implementation and strengthen cross-border collaboration under the SOCO initiative. The Togolese delegation included the Prefect of Tandjoari, Agbante Oukoure. The North East Regional Minister, Ibrahim Tia, called for stronger cooperation between Ghana and Togo to address emerging security threats, including violent extremism, cross-border crime and illicit arms trafficking. In a welcome address at the session, Mr Tia said the two countries shared longstanding historical, cultural, social and economic ties, particularly among communities along their common border. “These enduring ties constitute a valuable foundation upon which we can build stronger partnerships for peace, security, and sustainable development,” he said. He warned that instability in the Sahel region posed growing risks to border communities, stressing that Ghana’s relative peace and stability should not be taken for granted. Mr Tia said the SOCO Project was important not only for delivering infrastructure but also for strengthening social cohesion, improving livelihoods and enhancing communities’ resilience to conflict and other shocks. The World Bank-supported initiative is being implemented in Ghana, Togo, Benin and Côte d’Ivoire to strengthen social cohesion, improve socioeconomic and climate resilience, and reduce fragility, conflict and violence. In Ghana, the project covers 48 metropolitan, municipal and district assemblies across six beneficiary regions, including the North East Region. Its interventions include investments in education, healthcare, markets, water systems and livelihood activities, particularly for women and young people. Mr Tia noted that poverty, unemployment, social exclusion and competition over resources could fuel grievances that extremist and criminal groups might exploit. “Development must go beyond the provision of physical infrastructure. It must also empower communities, strengthen local institutions, promote inclusion, and create opportunities for people to participate meaningfully in their own development,” he said. He urged stakeholders to assess the project’s impact beyond the number of facilities constructed, focusing instead on service quality, improved livelihoods and the trust built among communities. “Our success must not be measured solely by the number of projects completed or facilities constructed. It must also be measured by the quality of services delivered, the livelihoods improved, the trust built among communities, and the contribution our interventions make towards lasting peace and stability,” he added. The working session, held under the project’s Regional Coordination and Dialogue Platform, aims to strengthen coordination, share lessons, review progress and identify challenges affecting implementation. Participants are also expected to engage communities in areas such as Nakpanduri and Bimbago to hear directly from beneficiaries, identify their concerns and assess the impact of project interventions. Mr Tia called for stronger collaboration among governments, implementing agencies and border communities, emphasising that no single country or institution could address the region’s security and development challenges alone.

Wontumi allegedly targeted in attempted poisoning in prison – Palgrave
items.description: A senior aide to former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has alleged that some prison inmates attempted to poison the politician. Dr Palgrave Boakye-Danquah explained that Mr Wontumi had informed him of the alleged incident when he appeared in court on Tuesday, adding that prison authorities had initiated investigations to establish the facts. “Chairman is okay. We haven’t received any medical reports from the doctors. But I have received indications that over the past week, some prison inmates attempted to poison him,” Dr Boakye-Danquah told Accra-based Citi FM as Mr Wontumi marked 100 days in prison. He stressed on Tuesday, October 27, that investigations were underway to verify the allegation. “And so I’ve been informed that there are some investigations that are ongoing to make sure that they verify the truth or otherwise of that,” he added. Dr Boakye-Danquah said he had also spoken to the prison commander, who assured him that the matter was being investigated. “He mentioned that to me today when he came to court, and I have spoken to the commander, and the commander said he has asked them to investigate the matter, so he will come back to me on that issue. This attempted poisoning of his life happened a few days ago,” he said. However, Dr Boakye-Danquah said no medical report had been received in connection with the claim, and the circumstances surrounding the alleged attempt remain under investigation.

Accidents de la circulation : 23 morts et 2.995 blessés en périmètre urbain, du 19 au 25 octobre
items.description: Vingt trois personnes ont trouvé la mort et 2.995 autres ont été blessées, dont 132 grièvement, dans 2.241 accidents de la circulation survenus en périmètre urbain durant la semaine allant du 19 au 25 octobre, a indiqué la Direction générale de la sûreté nationale (DGSN). Ces accidents sont principalement dus, dans l'ordre, à l'inadvertance des conducteurs, au non-respect de la priorité, à la non maîtrise du véhicule, à l'inadvertance des piétons, à l'excès de vitesse, au changement de direction non autorisé, au non-respect de la distance de sécurité, au changement de direction sans usage du clignotant, au non-respect du stop, au non-respect du feu rouge, à la circulation en sens interdit, à la conduite en état d’ébriété, à la circulation sur la voie gauche et au dépassement défectueux, a précisé la DGSN dans un communiqué. Concernant les opérations de contrôle et de répression en matière de circulation, les services de sûreté ont enregistré 52.459 contraventions, dressé 8.190 procès-verbaux transmis au Parquet et procédé au recouvrement de 44.269 amendes transactionnelles. Les sommes perçues au titre de ces contraventions ont atteint 9.524.900 dirhams, a ajouté le communiqué, faisant état de la mise en fourrière municipale de 5.606 véhicules, de la saisie de 8.190 documents et du retrait de la circulation de 509 véhicules. Netanyahu scrambles for votes as Israelis turn out in record numbers
items.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, fighting for his political life, scrambled to bring out his base on Tuesday as Israelis voted in record numbers in the country’s first election since the Oct 7, 2023 attack . With Israeli Arabs voters turning out in strong numbers, Netanyahu raised fears that leaders of the minority group were out to “steal the election” and reverse the hardline Jewish nationalist direction in which his government has taken the country. The first exit polls showed the opposition bloc with a slight edge over Netanyahu’s camp as voting ended, but still shy of an outright majority in the 120-seat Knesset. The country’s main pollsters — Channels 11, 12 and 13 — projected the opposition bloc to win 52 or 53 seats, and Netanyahu’s bloc to win 50, although his Likud would be the largest single party in the parliament, with 24 or 25 seats. Netanyahu’s Likud Party also unsuccessfully asked election authorities to keep polls open past 10pm (1am PKT), as the opposition charged that he was looking for pretexts to challenge the results. “We cannot leave this battle here in the hands of the left and the Arab parties that want to bring an end to the Jewish state,” a visibly tense Netanyahu told supporters as he tried to bring up turnout in a Likud stronghold. “So no barbecues, don’t go to the beach — go to the polling station and vote Likud,” he said. Nationwide turnout as of 6:00pm was 66.7 per cent, the highest at that point in the day since such statistics were first recorded in 1973, the Central Elections Committee said. Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of Oct 7 and the multi-front regional wars that it sparked, with the trauma from the attack still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign. The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by the war in Iran and the devastating military campaign in Gaza , soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank . In the years since Oct 7, 2023, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble , occupy southern Lebanon and pummel Iran with US help. The last opinion polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief. Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers. Before voting, the 66-year-old Eisenkot paid his respects privately at the grave of his son Gal, whose death fighting in Gaza has drawn empathy from many Israelis. Speaking afterwards at a polling station, Eisenkot called on Israelis to vote to replace “the worst government since the state was established”. Arab minority in spotlight Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with tens of thousands of Israelis estimated to have flown in from abroad for an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country. Eilana Zisblit, 55, told AFP she had travelled back from Canada, where she has lived for almost 30 years, to vote for a centre-right party in Eisenkot’s bloc. “The country is going in a really, really bad direction. Both for Jews and Arabs living in the country, and for Jews living abroad,” she said. The time to act is “now, or the country really won’t survive anymore”. Turnout appeared to be unusually high among Israeli Arabs and in east Jerusalem. Netanyahu, 77, has served as prime minister on and off for more than 19 years. Throughout his career, he has repeatedly raised the spectre of Arab voters as a threat. He warned on Tuesday of Arabs voting by the busload, writing on social media that Israel could wake up to a “government of the left wing and Muslim Brotherhood”. Netanyahu said that three senior officials of the United Arab List had been arrested with envelopes full of cash in the south. The acting director general of the Central Elections Committee, Dean Livne, said that police had “caught individuals who tried to bribe voters”, adding that the unidentified suspects were not at polling stations and were caught near their homes. He said the matter was a localised case and under investigation. United Arab List head Mansour Abbas , who could emerge as a kingmaker in a close election, accused Netanyahu of “lying and inciting” to mobilise his voters. In Tel Aviv, left-wing party The Democrats, which is part of Eisenkot’s opposition bloc, said police had arrested a man with a knife who had moved threateningly towards its leader Yair Golan. “Incitement and violence will not intimidate us,” Golan said in a statement, blaming the incident on the “poison machine” of Netanyahu. Trump endorsement Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket. Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot’s Yashar party and spanning from the right to the centre-left — including former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, as well as seasoned politician Avigdor Lieberman and left-leaning Golan. The Arab minority accounts for some 21pc of the population, but Eisenkot has been coy on whether he would ally with their lawmakers to wrest power from Netanyahu. Netanyahu has cast himself as the only person who can keep Israel safe. In the last days of the campaign, he posted an image of a nuclear bomb destroying Tel Aviv and talked up his endorsement by US President Donald Trump, who is also fond of alleging election fraud.

items.title: How Hubtel is rethinking AI in Ghana: Own your data, rent the intelligence
items.description: From the trader at Makola checking prices on her phone to the graduate in Kumasi searching for work, one question is getting louder across Ghana. Will artificial intelligence make life better, or will it take away what people already have? Ghana has placed its bet. In 2025 it launched a ten-year national AI strategy, and government has committed $270 million to get the country ready. But for ordinary Ghanaians, the most useful answers may come from a local company that has already tried, stumbled and found a smarter way forward. That company is Hubtel . Head of Engineering, Augustine Adjei, told the national audience during the premiere of the AI & Ghana’s documentary on Joy News, exactly what Ghana’s AI journey looks like from the inside, and why the country does not need to start big to win. About the Digital Economy Forum The Digital Economy Forum is a national thought-leadership platform conceived by Hubtel to create evidence-based conversations about the technologies, policies and ideas shaping Ghana’s economic future. It combines original documentary storytelling with a televised debate on JoyNews and Joy FM, bringing together government, regulators, businesses, academics and everyday Ghanaians. The maiden edition tackled digital fraud and why trust matters in Ghana’s growing digital economy. The latest edition asked a bigger question: AI and the Ghana economy, opportunity or disruption? For Hubtel, which helps Ghanaians pay bills, send money and order goods, the stakes are personal. A digital economy only grows when people trust it, understand it and can benefit from it. The forum is Hubtel’s way of making sure that conversation happens in public, with the facts on the table and ordinary people in the room. Opportunity or disruption? Both, says Hubtel Asked whether AI is good or bad news for Ghana, Augustine Adjei refused to pick one side. “It is both,” he said. “Growth is hard and painful, but the disruption is a setback while the opportunity is exponential.” He compared it to a catapult. You get pulled back first, and that painful pull is what launches you forward. Change will hurt in places, but those who prepare will move faster than ever. When Hubtel tried to build its own AI Hubtel opened an AI lab in 2023, before chat apps like ChatGPT became part of everyday life. It hired skilled Ghanaian engineers to build AI from scratch. The lab’s biggest project helped the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) catch power theft. The system flagged meters that seemed not to be paying, traced back through the records and connected the dots. Hubtel also built its own fraud detection and call-centre tools. Then the world moved faster and cheaper. By 2025, global AI companies were selling far more powerful tools for about $20 to $25 a month. Hubtel did what any smart trader does when a better product appears at a lower price. It stopped trying to outbuild the giants and started buying access. Talent Isn’t the Problem Augustine Adjei explained the decision with a picture every Ghanaian understands. “Would you want an Italian chef to cook your fufu and light soup, or an equally competent Ghanaian chef who has lived here all their life?” he asked. The answer is obvious: the Ghanaian chef. But training that chef takes time and money. Until then, you hire the chef who can feed you today while you plan for tomorrow. He was clear that Ghana’s problem has never been brains. “Talent is equally distributed; resources are not,” he said. Hubtel had the people. What it did not have was the hundreds of millions of dollars global firms spend on AI. Own your data, rent the engine Hubtel did not just sign up for a free chatbot. It negotiated directly with leading global AI companies, which were surprised a Ghanaian firm could pay at that level. Under the deal, Hubtel runs the AI inside its own systems, keeps full ownership of its data, and the providers have promised not to use Hubtel’s information to train their models. Augustine Adjei summed up the rule simply: “Own what you can before you scale.” He also shared a funny but serious warning. When Hubtel tested a free AI model and asked it about the company, the model said Hubtel was headquartered in Kigali. AI only knows what you teach it, so Ghanaians must feed it Ghanaian facts. The best example of this thinking is Hubtel’s virtual call centre. Because so many Ghanaians transact on Hubtel every day, the phones ring constantly. An AI agent now answers first and can check a customer’s order status on the spot. It works because all the information it needs already belongs to Hubtel. It is built in Ghana, trained on Ghanaian data and speaks to customers in a Ghanaian accent. For Augustine Adjei, that is the point. “AI is not a thing, it is us. There is no AI without humans,” he said. “If we are biased, AI will be biased.” Honorable Sam George backs the Hubtel approach Communications Minister of Ghana, Honorable Sam George said Hubtel’s story shows why Ghana must fix its data first. “AI models are only as good as their data sets,” he said. Hubtel had found no simple way for companies in Ghana to share data. The Minister said government is building a national data exchange hub to connect about 48 public registries, from the Ghana Health Service to the National Identification Authority, so developers make one request instead of 48. Companies are welcome to join, as long as they contribute data too. On jobs, he echoed Hubtel’s message that people must grow with the technology. “Those who evolve and adapt will survive,” he said. “Those who fail to evolve and adapt will fall off.” Bright Simmons of Imani Africa, the night’s toughest critic of government spending, held up Hubtel as an example of doing AI in the right order: use a proven global tool first, then build local. “If you don’t define your problem extremely well, AI can’t give you answers,” he warned, adding: “We should not stay on the surface.” Five lessons for every Ghanaian You do not need to be a tech company to learn from Hubtel. Whether you run a chop bar, a boutique or a small office, the same rules apply: Start with what you already have. Your customer list, your records and the way you work are your biggest AI asset. Use what works today. Global AI tools are cheap and powerful, so use them while local options grow. Guard your information. Keep control of your data and know where it goes. Teach the AI about Ghana. If a tool thinks Hubtel is in Kigali, it can get your business wrong too. Think before you upload. Augustine Adjei said his phone holds his 74-year-old mother’s medical record, and he would not run it through a public chatbot without protection. Ghana’s AI future will not be decided by one big announcement. It will be shaped by businesses and individuals who test, learn, adjust and keep going. Hubtel has shown a practical path for the whole country: own your data, rent the engine, solve real problems for real customers and keep your people learning. Through the Digital Economy Forum, it is making sure every Ghanaian gets to hear that conversation.

items.title: “It’s always been more of a friendship than music” – King Promise on his relationship with Mr Eazi
items.description: Ghanaian Afrobeats and Highlife singer-songwriter King Promise says his relationship with Nigerian singer and entrepreneur Mr Eazi has always been built on genuine friendship rather than music, revealing that the two have known each other for more than a decade. Speaking in an interview with Lexis Bill on Joy FM’s Drive Time on Tuesday, October 27, King Promise said their friendship dates back to around 2012, before either of them had a hit song. He recalled that he was still in school when they met, while Mr Eazi was working on his first mixtape, About to Blow , which preceded his breakthrough in music. “For us, it’s always been more of a friendship even than music,” King Promise said. He explained that the two rarely collaborated musically in the early stages of their relationship, but when they eventually made songs together, the results travelled far. “We barely made songs till we made songs. And then whenever we made them, they went far,” he said. King Promise said he values friendships that are not built around what the people involved can gain from each other professionally. He cited his relationships with music group R2Bees and rapper Sarkodie as similar examples, noting that he had known them for years before they worked together on songs. “I try to keep genuine friendships where it’s not because you need me and I need you,” he said. Beyond their friendship, King Promise credited Mr Eazi with influencing his outlook through his honesty, confidence and approach to business. “The influence he’s had on me is that he keeps it a thousand percent. He’s very real and straightforward, direct to the point. If he says yes, it’s yes and if he says no, he says no,” he said. He added that Mr Eazi’s confidence in his work and success in music had also inspired him, particularly when he was still establishing himself as an artiste. King Promise recalled watching Mr Eazi thrive in the industry while they exchanged ideas in the studio. “I was still coming when he was already flying. And that alone was a lot for me, like my guy is smashing it,” he said. The Terminator hitmaker also praised Mr Eazi’s business instincts, saying their conversations sometimes extend to investment opportunities, including stocks. He described Mr Eazi as a businessman whose entrepreneurial interests predated his music career. Mr Eazi, he explained, initially worked as a promoter and booked artistes before venturing into music and later establishing a record label. “It was business that even got him into music,” King Promise said, adding that his friend was a “forward thinker”.

items.title: Benjamin Larweh: Ghana’s cocoa farms must not become casualties of the gold rush
items.description: Ghana’s fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, has reached a critical juncture. As the government explores ways to formalise eligible artisanal and small-scale miners, a fundamental principle must remain non-negotiable: no economic activity should be permitted to destroy the agricultural assets, livelihoods and ecosystems upon which the country’s long-term prosperity depends. The Ghana Cocoa Board Act, 2026 (Act 1182), provides an important legal foundation for defending one of Ghana’s most valuable agricultural resources. By according cocoa farms protected status and establishing safeguards against mining and other prohibited extractive activities, including a reported 500-metre restriction around protected farms, the law reinforces a principle that should guide national development: the pursuit of mineral wealth must not come at the expense of agricultural sustainability. The challenge now is to translate that principle into effective enforcement. Protecting more than cocoa trees Cocoa is far more than an export commodity. It sustains hundreds of thousands of farming households, supports rural economies and contributes to Ghana’s international economic standing. Behind every productive cocoa farm lies years of labour, investment and accumulated agricultural knowledge. When illegal mining destroys such a farm, the loss extends beyond uprooted trees. It can deprive families of their principal source of income, degrade productive soil, threaten water resources and undermine the economic prospects of future generations. The damage may also extend beyond the immediate mining site. Excavation, erosion, altered drainage and potential contamination can affect neighbouring farms and communities. For Ghana, therefore, protecting cocoa farms is not simply an agricultural responsibility. It is an economic, environmental and social imperative. Act 1182 must mean what it says The enactment of Act 1182 creates an opportunity to strengthen the protection of cocoa farms against destructive activities. Its effectiveness, however, will depend on the clarity of its implementation and the consistency with which the law is enforced. The reported 500-metre restriction is particularly significant because the risks associated with mining are not always confined to the precise location of excavation. Activities close to cocoa farms can compromise their productivity and threaten surrounding ecosystems. To make this protection effective, the relevant authorities must establish reliable farm maps, clearly identify protected areas and ensure that proposed mining sites are screened against applicable restrictions before authorisations are granted. The Ghana Cocoa Board, mining regulators, environmental authorities, land administration institutions and local government must work together to prevent conflicting decisions and close enforcement gaps. A protected farm must not exist only on paper. Its protection must be visible in the security of the farmer, the integrity of the land and the continued productivity of the crop. Formalisation is not a licence to break the law Recent public debate surrounding comments by Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi has renewed attention to the government’s approach to unlicensed mining. There is a legitimate case for formalising eligible artisanal miners. Proper licensing, registration, environmental standards and regulatory oversight can improve accountability, support livelihoods and help move mining into the lawful economy. But formalisation must never be confused with permission to mine wherever an operator chooses. An unlicensed operation does not become lawful simply because it is economically beneficial or located outside a forest reserve or water body. Its eligibility for formalisation must be assessed under the applicable legal framework, including restrictions governing protected cocoa farms. A miner who qualifies for formalisation must still comply with every applicable law governing where mining may take place. This distinction is essential. Formalisation should create a pathway towards lawful mining, not an avenue for circumventing environmental safeguards or statutory prohibitions. Where mining is prohibited to protect cocoa farms, no administrative arrangement or economic justification should be used to override that restriction. The objective is not to demonise miners or dismiss the economic pressures facing mining communities. It is to ensure that legitimate economic opportunities are pursued within the law and without transferring unacceptable costs to farmers and the wider public. From legislation to enforcement Three priorities should guide implementation. First, with the already existing Cocoa Management System (CMS), Ghana can develop an authoritative, georeferenced register of protected cocoa farms to help regulators identify prohibited areas and verify compliance with the prescribed buffer. Second, enforcement must be consistent and evidence-based. Those responsible for illegal mining should be investigated and held accountable in accordance with the law, regardless of their political connections, financial influence or position in society. Third, COCOBOD can further strengthen the economic viability of cocoa farming through improved access to agricultural inputs, extension services, farm rehabilitation and effective support for farmers. Protecting cocoa farms requires both enforcement against unlawful destruction and sustained investment in the livelihoods that make farming worthwhile. These measures should complement a transparent formalisation programme that directs eligible miners towards lawful sites and requires compliance with environmental and licensing obligations. A national interest beyond partisan politics The protection of cocoa farms should not become another casualty of political disagreement. The government’s anti-galamsey policy must be assessed against clear standards: compliance with the law, effective environmental protection and measurable results for affected communities. Ghana must demonstrate that its commitment to responsible mining is compatible with its responsibility to protect agriculture. It must also assure international cocoa buyers, processors and development partners that the country is serious about safeguarding the land and communities that sustain its cocoa industry. The choice is not between gold and cocoa. It is between a development model that respects the limits of lawful economic activity and one that allows immediate commercial gains to undermine long-term national prosperity. Act 1182 provides an important foundation. The real test lies in its implementation. Ghana’s cocoa farms represent generations of investment and a vital source of rural livelihoods. Their destruction in the pursuit of gold would impose costs far greater than the value of the minerals recovered. The gold beneath Ghana’s soil may be valuable, but it must never become an excuse to destroy the cocoa farms that help sustain the nation.

Une réapparition qui redonne espoir aux militants de son parti Rewmi. Cheikh Guèye, fidèle du mouvement, attendait un message de son leader depuis deux ans. « Depuis 2024, on vivait dans le désespoir. Et avec ces déclarations, l’espoir est revenu », s’enthousiasme-t-il. Ses détracteurs lui reprochent de s’être rapproché du pouvoir après avoir quitté l’opposition. Pour beaucoup de ses partisans, il reste pourtant la référence de l’opposition. Ablaye Ndiaye, tee-shirt orange de Rewmi sur les épaules, met en avant son parcours et son expérience. « C’est le candidat idéal, il est là pour l’intérêt du pays. À part lui, sur qui on peut compter pour l’opposition ? » Certains se projettent déjà dans la prochaine échéance présidentielle. « On est prêts à l’accompagner pour l’élection prochaine », affirme Birane Lo, technicien venu lui aussi encourager Idrissa Seck. Une militante salue également un homme « qui a toujours mis les femmes en avant. items.title: Sokoto Assembly okays establishment of state police
items.description: The Sokoto State House of Assembly unanimously adopted the Sixth Alteration Bill, which seeks to provide a constitutional framework for establishing state police services in Nigeria. The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the Deputy Majority Leader of the House, Mustapha Abdullahi (APC-Sokoto South II), moved the motionduring plenary in Sokoto on Tuesday. Presenting the bill, Abdullahi said it sought to amend the 1999 Constitution, as altered, to establish state police services while retaining the Nigeria Police Force as the federal police service. He said the executive transmitted the bill, the Senate considered it on June 24, the House of Representatives on July 23, andthe Sokoto Assembly on September 22. According to him, the proposed framework will delineate the responsibilities of federal and state police services to ensure effective policing and address security challenges across the country. He explained that the federal police would handle interstate and international crimes, terrorism, cybercrime, border security, policing of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and protection of federal assets. “Conversely, state police services would be responsible for law enforcement, maintenance of public order and safety, protection of lives and property, and investigation of local crimes. “Therefore, the federal police and state police will function side-by-side in every state,” Abdullahi said. The lawmaker added that the federal police could intervene in state policing matters at the request of a state governor or where there was a breakdown of law and order that the state police could not contain. He said the head of a state police service would be known as the State Commander of Police and appointed by the governor on the recommendation of the National Police Council, subject to confirmation by the State House of Assembly. Abdullahi further explained that the bill proposed the establishment of a State Police Service Commission as an executive body responsible for the appointment, promotion and discipline of state police personnel, except the State Commander. On funding, the lawmaker said the proposed framework would provide for the State Police Service Commission to receive funds directly from the state’s Consolidated Revenue Fund to ensure financial autonomy. He added that the Nigeria Police Force would continue to operate in every state until the state’s police service commenced operations. Abdullahi cited Section 9(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a constitutional alteration must be approved by resolutions of the houses of assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states. Contributing to the debate, several lawmakers supported the bill, describing state policing as a necessary measure to address the security challenges confronting states across the country. The Speaker, Alhaji Tukur Bala, who presided over the plenary, subsequently put the motion to a voice vote and the lawmakers unanimously adopted it. items.title: South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release
items.description: — Insist on leadership rotation to Abia, urge massive voter turnout By Steve Oko The South-East Traditional Rulers Council has renewed its demand for the unconditional release of detained Indigenous People of Biafra, IPOB, leader, Mazi Nnamdi Kanu, lamenting that previous appeals to the Federal Government have failed to yield the desired outcome. The monarchs also reaffirmed their position that the council’s leadership should rotate to Abia State, with HRM Eze Sir Dr Linus Nto Mbah assuming the chairmanship in accordance with the council’s constitution. These resolutions were contained in a communiqué issued after the council’s quarterly delegates meeting held on October 23, 2026, at the Parliament of Ndi Eze, Owerri, Imo State. On the political front, the traditional rulers expressed concern over the scheduled dates for the forthcoming national elections, which they said could pose challenges for the South-East. They nevertheless urged eligible voters across the region to return to their respective registration areas and participate massively in the elections. The council also called on traditional rulers and community leaders to suspend festivals and ceremonies during the election period to enable eligible voters to exercise their civic responsibilities. On traditional leadership in the South, the monarchs reaffirmed their support for the rotational chairmanship of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council among the South-East, South-West and South-South geopolitical zones. They rejected any arrangement that would confer permanent chairmanship on one zone, insisting that the position should rotate among the three zones for two-year terms, in line with the decision of the Southern Governors Forum reached in Ogun State in 2025. The council further called for the reconstitution of the Southern Traditional Rulers Council’s leadership to reflect recognised traditional rulers from member states and conform to the leadership template of the Southern Governors Forum. The communiqué was signed by the chairman of the South-East Traditional Rulers Council and chairman of the Abia State Council of Traditional Rulers, HRM Eze Dr Linus Nto Mbah; the Obi of Onitsha, HRM Igwe Nnaemeka Achebe; and other traditional rulers from the five South-East states. The monarchs expressed appreciation to Imo State Governor, Senator Hope Uzodimma, for hosting the meeting, as well as the Imo State Council of Traditional Rulers and the people of the state for their hospitality. They also acknowledged the support and encouragement of governors across the South-East. The post South-East monarchs renew demand for Nnamdi Kanu’s release appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: How we will curb election violence – INEC
items.description: .Vows to hunt down anyone who threatens ad-hoc staff, corps members .Set to hold National Election Security Confab By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved. INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured. The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres. Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence. He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive. The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter. The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges. According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members. Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution. “Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the full weight of the law. He disclosed that the Commission would shortly convene a National Election Security Conference in Abuja, where state-specific security protocols for high-risk zones would be finalised. Amupitan acknowledged that the North-East presents distinct operational challenges, including vast desert terrains, riverine stretches along the Benue trough, remote agrarian communities and expansive landmasses. He noted, however, that the zone had demonstrated remarkable resilience and civic determination. The zone has 13,965,475 registered voters, representing 13.51 per cent of the national register of over 103 million. Bauchi State has the highest number with 3,012,547 voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. The Chairman said the 2027 General Election would be a simultaneous national undertaking across 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The Presidential and National Assembly Elections are scheduled for Saturday, 16th January 2027, while the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly Elections will hold on Saturday, 6th February 2027. Earlier, the host Resident Electoral Commissioner REC for Gombe State, Alhaji Umar Muktar Gajiram, speaking on behalf of all North-East RECs, assured the Chairman that the zone was fully prepared, loyal and committed to ensuring that not a single voter out of the 13.96 million in the zone is disenfranchised. Gajiram said all directives on voter register display, logistics audit and technological testing would be executed to the letter. Amupitan assured staff and stakeholders across the North-East that INEC was not working in isolation, describing security as “the bedrock of electoral integrity.” “Insecurity may pose a challenge, but our collective constitutional resolve is far stronger,” he said. items.title: Forum des pays exportateurs de gaz : Poutine dénonce les conséquences des sanctions occidentales et appelle à renforcer la coopération énergétique
items.description: Vladimir Poutine a appele, le 27 octobre a Moscou, les pays exportateurs de gaz a renforcer leur cooperation pour retablir la stabilite d'un marche mondial affecte par les conflits, les sanctions et les perturbations des approvisionnements. Le president russe s'exprimait lors du 8e sommet du Forum des pays exportateurs de gaz (FPEG), reunissant notamment des representants de l'Iran, du Qatar, du Mozambique, de la Guinee equatoriale et de la Libye. Les membres de cette organisation concentrent 70 % des reserves mondiales de gaz naturel et environ 40 % de ses exportations. Devant les participants, Vladimir Poutine a souligne que d'importants volumes de gaz avaient disparu du marche malgre une demande toujours soutenue. Il a evoque les tensions au Moyen-Orient, les obstacles aux echanges energetiques et la destruction des gazoducs Nord Stream, qu'il a qualifiee d'« actes terroristes ». Le president russe a particulierement denonce les tentatives visant a exclure son pays du marche gazier mondial. Selon lui, ces restrictions imposent des coûts considerables aux entreprises et aux consommateurs etrangers. Il a egalement critique la politique de l'Union europeenne, estimant que l'abandon des hydrocarbures russes et la rupture des contrats a long terme portent directement prejudice a l'industrie et a la population europeennes. « Ne creuse pas de fosse pour autrui, sinon tu y tomberas toi-meme », a-t-il declare, reprenant un proverbe pour illustrer les consequences de ces decisions. La Russie met en avant ses capacites energetiques et technologiques Vladimir Poutine a rappele la place de la Russie parmi les principaux acteurs du marche mondial du gaz : le pays dispose des plus importantes reserves de gaz naturel au monde et occupe le deuxieme rang pour la production. Reaffirmant la volonte de Moscou de demeurer un fournisseur fiable et previsible, il a mis en avant les progres realises dans le developpement de technologies nationales, notamment celles du gaz naturel liquefie (GNL), deja utilisees dans les conditions difficiles de l'Arctique. Ces capacites prennent une importance particuliere dans un contexte de hausse attendue de la consommation mondiale. La demande de gaz, qui a atteint 4 200 milliards de metres cubes en 2025, pourrait s'elever a 5 500 milliards d'ici 2050. Des propositions russes pour stabiliser le marche mondial Face a ces perspectives, Vladimir Poutine a propose d'intensifier la cooperation entre producteurs, d'exploiter de nouveaux gisements et de moderniser les infrastructures. Il a insiste sur le role du GNL, qui represente pres de la moitie du commerce mondial de gaz et offre une plus grande souplesse dans les livraisons. Le president russe a toutefois rappele que ces projets necessitent des investissements considerables et des garanties a long terme. Soulignant que la flambee des prix ne profite pas necessairement aux producteurs, il a defendu la stabilite du marche et les contrats durables. Il a egalement appele a la fin des conflits et a la levee des sanctions afin de favoriser les investissements energetiques. Moscou propose par ailleurs de renforcer la coordination entre pays exportateurs pour anticiper les crises et les menaces contre les infrastructures gazieres. Vladimir Poutine a reaffirme la disponibilite de la Russie a partager ses technologies et a developper de nouveaux partenariats. Il a notamment annonce que Moscou etudiait les possibilites d'une cooperation avec les etats-Unis dans l'Arctique.

items.title: Cameroon suspends opposition party
items.description: Authorities have suspended the Cameroon National Salvation Front (FSNC) of opposition figure Issa Tchiroma Bakary, in Gambian exile, for three months, the minister for territorial administration announced Tuesday. Bakary, a former minister, had rallied young people seeking change during the presidential election of a year ago, won by 93-year-old Paul Biya, who has been in power since 1982. Territorial administration minister Paul Atanga Nji suspended the party, according to a statement, on grounds of “incitement to insurrection” and “serious disturbance of public order,” saying this had occurred “before, during and after the presidential election of October 12, 2025.” The statement warned the party could face legal challenge if it did not accept the sanction. After declaring himself the winner of the election, Bakary repeatedly called on supporters to defend his “victory”, triggering protests in major cities that were brutally suppressed, resulting in a number of deaths with the government yet to provide a toll. Thereafter Bakary went into exile in Gambia. The temporary suspension of the party, which has two members of parliament, comes ahead of local and parliamentary elections, scheduled for early 2027 after multiple postponements. The post Cameroon suspends opposition party appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Embouteillages : un étudiant conçoit le premier indice de congestion urbaine en Algérie
items.description: Une plateforme permettant d’être informé en temps réel des niveaux de congestion du trafic routier dans 27 villes algériennes vient d’être mise au point par un étudiant de l’ESTIN (l’École supérieure en sciences et Technologies de l’Informatique et du Numérique) de Bejaïa. En effet, Takieddine Rehail, étudiant en 3e année du second cycle (3CS) à l’ESTIN, a mis au point Algerian Urban Congestion Index, une plateforme qui sert à mesurer et à analyser la congestion routière dans 27 agglomérations algériennes, dont Alger, Oran, Bejaïa, Djelfa, Boumerdès, Constantine, Blida et Tlemcen, à partir des données de trafic accessibles sur Google Maps, sans recourir à des capteurs physiques. Une grande fierté pour son encadreur ainsi que pour l’établissement où il est scolarisé en interne. Embouteillages : un étudiant de Bejaïa crée un outil de surveillance Takieddine Rehail est né en 2004 à Constantine. Étudiant à l’École supérieure en sciences et Technologies de l’Informatique et du Numérique (ESTIN) de Bejaïa, il a développé une plateforme innovante dédiée à l’analyse de la congestion routière en Algérie. Ce projet met en lumière le potentiel des jeunes talents algériens dans le domaine du numérique et leur capacité à concevoir des solutions technologiques répondant à des problématiques concrètes. En mai dernier, le professeur Faïcal Azouaou, son enseignant et mentor, a proposé un stage d’été pour ses étudiants. L’idée était de concevoir un indice de congestion urbaine pour les villes algériennes qui souffrent grandement d’un trafic routier dense, sans qu’aucun outil local ne permette de les comparer objectivement. « Ce stage visait à construire le premier prototype d’indice de congestion pour le contexte algérien, à partir de données via API de cartographie ou du traitement des images de trafic de Google Maps », explique à TSA Nesrine Mitouche, chargée de communication à l’ESTIN de Bejaïa. Une plateforme pour comparer les villes plus touchées par la congestion Ce projet a été développé en collaboration avec le laboratoire LITAN, sous la houlette du professeur Faïçal Azouaou, enseignant à l’ESTIN. « La plateforme créée permet notamment de comparer les niveaux de congestion entre les villes et d’observer leur évolution selon les heures de la journée », indique encore Nesrine Mitouche. Une plateforme d’analyse du trafic routier est un système informatique qui permet de collecter, surveiller et analyser les données de circulation des véhicules afin de mieux comprendre le trafic, de détecter les embouteillages et d’améliorer la sécurité et la fluidité des déplacements. Des données qui peuvent être directement exploitées par les autorités locales, les urbanistes et les ingénieurs en transport afin de répondre à des problèmes de mobilité. Ces informations permettent également de repérer les ralentissements, les zones congestionnées et les variations du trafic selon les heures de la journée. Ce jeune étudiant mérite d’être encouragé et soutenu. Il incarne parfaitement cette jeunesse talentueuse, capable de faire preuve d’innovation, de créativité et d’ingéniosité. L’article Embouteillages : un étudiant conçoit le premier indice de congestion urbaine en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Ballon d’Or africain : Pape Gueye assume ses ambitions
items.description: Dans un entretien accordé à Canal+ Sport Afrique, dans l’émission « Talents d’Afrique » du lundi 26 octobre 2026, le milieu de terrain sénégalais Pape Gueye revient sur son épanouissement à Villarreal, sa mise en retrait temporaire de la sélection après le Mondial et son ambition de remporter le Ballon d’Or africain. Pape Gueye affiche ses ambitions. Après une saison marquée par la victoire du Sénégal à la Coupe d’Afrique des nations (CAN), au cours de laquelle il a inscrit le but décisif en finale, le milieu de terrain de Villarreal assume sa candidature au Ballon d’Or africain. Dans un entretien exclusif accordé à Canal+ Sport Afrique, le joueur sénégalais revient également sur son parcours récent et son attachement à l’équipe nationale. En Espagne, l’international sénégalais dit avoir trouvé un environnement favorable à son épanouissement. Après trois années passées à Villarreal, il assure se sentir bien au sein du club, où il bénéficie de la confiance de ses dirigeants et de bonnes conditions de travail. Sollicité par d’autres équipes lors du dernier mercato estival, il a choisi de poursuivre son aventure avec le club espagnol. « J’ai retrouvé mon meilleur niveau ici », explique-t-il, convaincu d’évoluer dans une équipe ambitieuse, capable de jouer les premières places et de se mesurer aux grandes formations européennes. Son objectif est de poursuivre sa progression et de contribuer aux ambitions de Villarreal. La CAN remportée avec le Sénégal a également marqué un tournant dans sa carrière. Le milieu de terrain estime que son but en finale a changé le regard porté sur lui, aussi bien au Sénégal qu’en Europe. Il raconte notamment avoir reçu les félicitations de joueurs du Real Madrid après cette rencontre, preuve, selon lui, de l’écho suscité par cette finale. « J’ai réagi sous le coup de l’émotion » L’entretien a également été l’occasion pour Pape Gueye de revenir sur sa décision de se mettre en retrait de la sélection nationale à l’issue de la Coupe du monde. Le joueur explique avoir beaucoup investi dans sa préparation pour cette compétition, avec l’ambition d’être au meilleur de sa forme pour servir son pays. Il évoque notamment les difficultés rencontrées dans la préparation, des tensions internes et sa frustration après avoir été remplacé assez tôt lors du match contre la Belgique, suivi de la défaite sénégalaise. « Je suis humain, c’était la goutte de trop et j’ai réagi sous le coup de l’émotion », reconnaît-il. Le milieu de terrain affirme toutefois avoir tourné cette page. Avec le recul, il considère cet épisode comme une expérience qui lui a permis de grandir. Il entend désormais regarder vers l’avenir et contribuer à écrire de nouvelles pages de l’histoire du football sénégalais. Pape Gueye insiste aussi sur la nécessité d’accompagner la nouvelle génération, qu’il juge particulièrement talentueuse. Il souligne l’importance de l’encadrement et des conseils du nouveau sélectionneur, dont il apprécie notamment l’expérience à son poste de milieu de terrain. Pour le joueur de Villarreal, l’objectif collectif reste clair : rendre fiers les Sénégalais et tout mettre en œuvre pour remporter la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des nations. Un Ballon d’Or africain dans le viseur Sur le plan individuel, Pape Gueye ne cache pas son ambition. Après une saison au cours de laquelle il affirme avoir atteint plusieurs objectifs, notamment sur le plan collectif, il considère légitime de figurer parmi les candidats au Ballon d’Or africain. « Au début de saison, je note toujours mes objectifs de buts, de passes décisives, de matchs joués, de trophées collectifs et individuels, et le Ballon d’Or africain faisait partie de mes objectifs », confie-t-il, tout en rappelant que le choix appartient aux votants. Le Sénégalais évoque également les deux compatriotes qui ont déjà remporté cette distinction, El-Hadji Diouf et Sadio Mané, qu’il considère comme des légendes du football national. Remporter à son tour ce trophée représenterait, selon lui, une immense fierté et l’aboutissement d’un parcours marqué par des moments difficiles. En attendant le verdict, Pape Gueye entend poursuivre sa progression en club et rester mobilisé pour la sélection. Entre ambitions individuelles et objectifs collectifs, le milieu sénégalais affiche sa volonté de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa carrière. Cheikh Tidiane NDIAYE

items.title: Burkina | Réformes éducatives : Le ministre Dingara explique les nouvelles orientations aux acteurs du Guiriko
items.description: Dans le cadre des réformes éducatives engagées par le gouvernement, le ministre de l'Enseignement de base, de l'Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des langues nationales, Jacques Sosthène Dingara, a rencontré les acteurs du système éducatif de la région du Guiriko, le mardi 27 octobre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso. Cette rencontre s'inscrit dans une tournée de suivi qui se déroule du 27 au 29 octobre dans les régions du Guiriko, du Bankuy et du Nando. Le système éducatif burkinabè est en pleine mutation. En effet, le Gouvernement a entamé une vaste reforme visant à intégrer la prise en compte des réalités spécifiques et culturelles du Burkina Faso dans l'enseignement de base. Pour mieux faire comprendre ce choix aux acteurs concernés, le ministre de l'Enseignement de base, de l'Alphabétisation et de la Promotion des langues nationales, Jacques Sosthène Dingara, a entamé une tournée d'échanges. Celle-ci intervient dans le prolongement du lancement du pacte NEKRE, le 17 octobre dernier, par le président du Faso. Selon le ministre Jacques Sosthène Dingara, cette initiative traduit la volonté des autorités de bâtir un système éducatif davantage ancré dans les réalités nationales, les valeurs endogènes Selon Jacques Sosthène Dingara, cette initiative traduit la volonté des autorités de bâtir un système éducatif davantage ancré dans les réalités nationales, les valeurs endogènes et l'identité culturelle du Burkina Faso. « Il nous a été donné instruction de travailler, dans les années à venir, à endogénéiser davantage notre système éducatif », a-t-il indiqué, soulignant la nécessité de former des citoyens fiers de leur identité et de leurs racines. Quatre réformes majeures pour l'année scolaire 2026-2027 La première réforme concerne la généralisation de l'enseignement bilingue. Désormais, les élèves de toutes les classes de cours préparatoire première année (CP1) commencent leurs apprentissages en lecture et en écriture dans leur langue maternelle. Lire aussi : Région des Koulsé : Le Premier ministre lance le Pacte Nekré pour refonder l’école burkinabè La deuxième porte sur l'éducation inclusive. Elle vise à garantir l'accès à l'éducation aux enfants à besoins spécifiques, notamment à travers le développement de l'apprentissage du braille dans chaque région et de la langue des signes dans chaque province. Soilliou Karantao saluant la tenue de cette rencontre, qu'il considère comme un cadre d'échanges et d'orientation essentiel pour les acteurs éducatifs La troisième réforme concerne la décolonisation des savoirs. Elle se traduit par la révision des curricula et des fiches pédagogiques afin de mieux valoriser les pratiques, les connaissances et les références culturelles nationales dans les enseignements dispensés aux élèves. Enfin, la quatrième réforme porte sur la réglementation des frais de scolarité. Cette première année de mise en œuvre doit permettre d'évaluer son application sur le terrain, d'identifier les éventuelles dérives et d'apporter les mesures correctives nécessaires. Harmoniser les pratiques pour améliorer la qualité Les échanges avec les encadreurs pédagogiques, les directeurs d'école, les enseignants et les responsables des structures éducatives déconcentrées et centrales visent à dresser un bilan des acquis, à relever les difficultés rencontrées et à dégager des perspectives d'amélioration. Pour le ministre, il est essentiel d'harmoniser les pratiques et de donner aux acteurs les orientations nécessaires à une application cohérente des réformes. Un aperçu des acteurs du monde éducatif Par cette démarche, le ministère entend consolider les transformations engagées et améliorer durablement la qualité de l'éducation au Burkina Faso, en cohérence avec les ambitions de souveraineté et de valorisation des savoirs endogènes portées par les autorités. Le directeur régional de l'Éducation préscolaire, primaire et non formelle (DREPPNF) du Guiriko, Soilliou Karantao, a pour sa part salué la tenue de cette rencontre, qu'il considère comme un cadre d'échanges et d'orientation essentiel pour les acteurs éducatifs. Il a réaffirmé l'engagement des responsables régionaux à s'approprier les recommandations formulées et à veiller à la mise en œuvre effective des décisions issues des travaux, afin de garantir une application harmonisée des réformes dans la région. items.title: Govt raises threshold for currency transaction reports to Rs3m as anti-money laundering framework reviewed
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The government has enhanced the currency transaction threshold by 50pc to Rs3 million for banks to trigger suspicious reports to the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU) of the State Bank of Pakistan under the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA). The increase in threshold from Rs2m to Rs3m for Currency Transaction Reports (CTRs) under the framework for analysing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) and CTRs was approved by the National Executive Committee (NEC) on Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism (AML-CFT). An STR is reported when a suspicious transaction or activity involving money laundering and terrorism financing is indicated. However, a CTR is required to be reported when a cash transaction is equal to or exceeds the specified threshold — now raised to Rs3m. The NEC, led by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, is responsible for setting limits for banks, financial institutions or other agencies dealing with financial transactions to generate CTRs and STRs on the amount of currency transactions through notifications in the official Gazette. It serves as a strategic forum for strengthening Pakistan’s AML-CFT framework and ensuring timely coordination, inter-agency cooperation and consistent monitoring for effective implementation of the measures discussed. The committee also approved the inclusion of Section 28 of the Pakistan Maritime Zones Act 2023 in Schedule I of the AMLA, meaning that maritime piracy has been covered as a predicate offence. Section 28 of the Maritime Zones Act 2023 defines “piracy” as any illegal act of violence, detention or depredation committed for private ends by the crew or the passengers of a private ship or a private aircraft and directed against another ship or aircraft or against persons or property onboard. The NEC also approved the inclusion of the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (PVARA) in Schedule IV of the AMLA, meaning that the crypto body would also have regulatory powers over virtual and digital assets to meet AML-CFT requirements, like the SBP, Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan and Federal Board of Revenue, among others. Under the AMLA, the FMU is designated to receive STRs and CTRs from reporting entities, analyse them and, if need be, seek the entire record and information related to the transaction in question from any agency or individual in Pakistan. All agencies and individuals are bound to promptly provide the requested record and information to enable the FMU to share its analysis on a confidential basis with the concerned investigating or prosecuting agencies, or with the financial intelligence units of other countries to make reciprocal arrangements to share, request and receive information relating to money laundering, the financing of terrorism and other offences. An official statement said the meeting reviewed compliance with its past decisions and progress on Pakistan’s AML-CFT regime, including the performance of the FMU, institutional capacity and initiatives involving artificial intelligence and machine learning. Aurangzeb emphasised the importance of regular and timely follow-up and stronger coordination among the relevant institutions to ensure effective implementation of the national AML-CFT framework. He also called for strengthening the FMU’s analytical and operational capacity through a clear implementation roadmap with defined timelines. The NEC also highlighted the importance of keeping Pakistan’s AML-CFT framework responsive to evolving financial risks and emerging technologies, while strengthening the analytical capabilities of relevant institutions.

items.title: Colère sociale en France : «le compte n’y est pas», estiment les syndicats enseignants
items.description: « On ressort de cette reunion avec la confirmation que le compte n'y est pas, sur la question des salaires notamment », a declare ce 27 octobre a une equipe de BFMTV la secretaire generale du syndicat enseignant SNES-FSU Sophie Venetitay, au sortir d'une reunion avec le ministre de l'education nationale edouard Geffray. Pour l'heure, le gouvernement Lecornu prevoit la suppression de 1 588 postes d'enseignants pour la prochaine rentree scolaire. C'est « absolument inacceptable », a ajoute la representante syndicale, apres avoir fustige un « declassement salarial tres important » qu'aurait essuye le personnel de l'education nationale, que « tout soit renvoye au debat parlementaire », et d'evoquer un appel a la greve le 5 novembre. Une journee de mobilisation, et de greves, « pour les salaires, les services publics, l'emploi et l'industrie », annoncee debut octobre par une intersyndicale reunissant la CFDT, la CGT, FO, l'UNSA et la FSU. La veille, les syndicats etudiants et lyceens, recus par le Premier ministre, avaient exprime leur mecontentement a l'egard des mesures proposees et ont appele a poursuivre la mobilisation les 31 octobre et 5 novembre. « Tout n'est pas encore satisfait et nous irons au bout », avait lance Louis Letoublon, vice-president de l'organisation « Les Lyceens ! » « Nous, ce qu'on demande, ce n'est pas plus de transparence. C'est-a-dire qu'on ne veut pas mieux savoir comment on est selectionne. Ce qu'on veut, c'est tout simplement ne plus etre selectionne », a lance le co-secretaire general de l'Union syndicale lyceenne Marius Menil, qui veut en finir avec la plateforme d'orientation Parcoursup. « On ne fera, dit-il, aucun compromis ».
