items.title: KabuteyMyMc and The Wuushman set November 6 for 100DegreesX 2.0
items.description: Accra’s live entertainment scene is gearing up for another dose of music, nostalgia and high-energy performances as event host Kabutey Ocansey, popularly known as Kabutey My Mc, teams up with The Wuushman for the second edition of 100DegreesX. Scheduled for Friday, November 6, 2026, at The Underbridge Annex in East Legon, Accra, 100DegreesX 2.0 follows a successful debut at the National Theatre in October 2025, where the duo treated patrons to a carefully curated musical experience featuring themed DJ sets, live performances and nostalgic moments. Unlike conventional concerts built around a succession of artiste performances, 100DegreesX places the relationship between the DJ and the master of ceremonies at the centre of the show. The concept blends music, storytelling, audience interaction, and themed segments to create a continuous entertainment experience. View this post on Instagram A post shared by 100DegreesX (@100degreesx) A debut filled with music and nostalgia The maiden edition offered a mix of musical styles and memorable appearances, setting the tone for the event’s return. The evening opened with a happy hour session featuring DJ Adom and MC Dave Lamptey before performances by Violin Boyfriend, Fati Music, and GG Brass warmed up the audience with a blend of live instrumentation and vocals. Actor Adjetey Annan added a nostalgic touch by opening the main show in character as Pusher, his memorable role in the popular 1990s television series Things We Do for Love . Kabutey My Mc and The Wuushman then took audiences through a two-hour musical journey featuring distinct themes. A gospel music segment gave way to an energetic jama session inspired by the morale culture associated with secondary school sporting events and university life. The duo also revisited Ghana’s political music history, playing popular campaign songs spanning different election seasons from 1992 to the present. Another segment honoured late Ghanaian musicians whose songs continue to resonate with audiences, featuring music associated with Ebony, Castro, and Daddy Lumba. One of the night’s biggest surprises was the appearance of highlife legend Kojo Antwi, whose performance of his much-loved song ‘Enfa Me Nkohor’ sparked an enthusiastic response from patrons. The show ended with a celebratory jam before DJ Vyrusky and MC Myster Pratt took over for the afterparty. What to expect from 100DegreesX 2.0 The second edition will once again put Kabutey My Mc and The Wuushman at the heart of the experience, building on a format that combines music selection, stagecraft, and audience participation. While the full lineup for this year’s event has yet to be announced in the information released by the organizers, the maiden edition established a format that moves beyond conventional DJ sets by weaving together familiar songs, cultural references and different musical eras. The concept also highlights the role DJs and MCs can play as creative performers in their own right, shaping the mood of an event and connecting audiences through music and shared memories. Tickets and reservations 100DegreesX 2.0 takes place on Friday, November 6, 2026, at The Underbridge Annex in East Legon, Accra. Regular tickets cost GH¢300 and are available by dialling * 928 *12#. For patrons seeking a VIP experience, organisers have announced that only 20 VIP tables are available. Reservations can be made via WhatsApp on 0262379854. With its second edition approaching, 100DegreesX is looking to build on the musical variety and audience engagement that defined its debut. For Accra’s music lovers, November 6 offers another opportunity to experience a show that puts the DJ and MC partnership firmly in the spotlight.

items.title: Prison reforms: Wontumi proposes dedicated prison hospital, conjugal visits for inmates
items.description: Former New Patriotic Party (NPP) Ashanti Regional Chairman, Bernard Antwi Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, has called for sweeping reforms in Ghana’s prisons, including the establishment of a dedicated prison hospital, improved welfare for prison officers and the introduction of conjugal visits for inmates. His proposals follow what he describes as a period of deep reflection and first-hand exposure to prison conditions, officers and inmates since his conviction in July 2026. Chairman Wontumi argues that Ghana’s correctional system must move beyond punishment to focus on rehabilitation, welfare and productivity, insisting that the country’s prisons require significant structural and institutional improvements. He said the system had seen little structural improvement since 1962 and called for a renewed national conversation on how inmates are treated and prepared for life after incarceration. “Not all prisoners are prisoners,” he said, stressing the need to distinguish between offenders and to ensure that the correctional system serves its intended purpose of reform. One of the key areas he highlighted is the welfare and remuneration of prison officers, arguing that their working conditions must be addressed as part of broader efforts to improve the service. He is also proposing a dedicated prison hospital to provide healthcare for inmates, alongside improved infrastructure and better conditions within the country’s correctional facilities. On inmate management, Chairman Wontumi called for a proper classification system to prevent minor offenders from being held alongside persons convicted of serious crimes, including armed robbery. He also raised concerns about the circumstances of young male inmates, particularly those aged between 18 and 35 who are incarcerated in connection with defilement cases. He argued that prolonged incarceration without adequate counselling and rehabilitation could expose inmates to further social and behavioural challenges. He is therefore advocating stronger counselling services and appropriate classification to address the different needs and circumstances of inmates. Chairman Wontumi further proposed improved family visitation arrangements, including designated spaces where children can visit their parents and other relatives in prison in a more suitable environment. He also called for the expansion of prison agriculture and improvements in infrastructure, suggesting that rehabilitation should include productive activities that can help inmates develop skills and prepare for reintegration into society. To drive the proposed changes, he wants the Speaker of Parliament to lead discussions on prison reform, with both the Majority and Minority sides working together to ensure that proposals considered by Parliament translate into concrete action. He has also called on the parliamentary select committees on Defence and Interior, as well as Health, and Food, Agriculture and Cocoa Affairs, to undertake working visits to prisons across the country to assess conditions first-hand. According to him, such visits would allow the committees to identify the challenges facing inmates and prison officers and recommend practical measures to improve the correctional system. Chairman Wontumi said his experience since July had led him to question whether Ghana’s prisons were adequately fulfilling their rehabilitative role, arguing that urgent reforms were needed to make the system more effective.

items.title: Le Maroc progresse dans le classement continental de l’attractivité des investissements de RMB
items.description: Le Maroc a réalisé une progression remarquable en se hissant au quatrième rang des destinations d’investissement les plus attractives du continent africain, porté par des années d’industrialisation et une croissance économique plus rapide, a indiqué la banque Rand Merchant Bank (RMB), filiale du groupe financier sud-africain FirstRand. « Le Maroc est le seul pays à progresser dans le top cinq du classement, dépassant l’Afrique du Sud pour s’emparer de la quatrième place », précise le rapport Where to Invest in Africa 2026/2027 de RMB, publié mardi. La performance du Maroc s’explique principalement par la dynamique de croissance, poursuit le document, qui fait état d’une progression du PIB de 4,9% pour le Maroc en 2025. L’inflation au Maroc est restée inférieure à 3% entre 2024 et la mi-2026, contre une moyenne de 5% en Afrique du Sud au cours des cinq années achevées en juin 2026. La transformation industrielle du Maroc constitue l’un des principaux moteurs de cette performance supérieure. Au cours de la décennie précédente, la production automobile marocaine avait presque doublé, passant de moins de 290.000 unités en 2015, à mesure que les usines Renault de Tanger et Stellantis de Kénitra augmentaient leurs capacités. À l’échelle de l’ensemble du secteur automobile, poursuit le rapport, les exportations marocaines de véhicules et de composants ont atteint un record de 157,6 milliards de dh (environ 15,7 milliards USD) en 2024, en hausse de 6,3% sur un an. Elles ont ainsi conservé leur place de premier secteur exportateur du Royaume, devant les phosphates et l’agriculture. Les entrées nettes d’investissements directs étrangers (IDE) au Maroc ont également enregistré une reprise sur deux ans. Selon les données de la Conférence des Nations unies sur le commerce et le développement (CNUCED), ces flux nets ont atteint près de 1,7 milliard en 2024, puis 3,3 milliards en 2025, soit une hausse de 91% sur un an. « Les entrées nettes d’IDE ont ainsi presque triplé par rapport à leur point bas de 2023, retrouvant des niveaux parmi les plus élevés jamais enregistrés », explique le document. Le tourisme a également contribué à renforcer cette dynamique, le Maroc ayant accueilli 19,8 millions de visiteurs en 2025 et engrangé des recettes touristiques de 124 milliards de dh, soit environ 13 milliards USD, au cours des onze premiers mois de l’année. Ces deux indicateurs ont atteint des niveaux historiques, les recettes ayant progressé de 19% sur un an. La RMB rappelle que le Maroc, qui coorganisera la Coupe du monde de football 2030 avec l’Espagne et le Portugal, prévoit d’investir environ 5 milliards USD dans les infrastructures liées à cet événement et vise 26 millions de touristes par an d’ici à la fin de la décennie. Dans sa consultation de mars 2026 au titre de l’article IV consacrée au Maroc, le Fonds monétaire international (FMI) a estimé le déficit budgétaire du Royaume à 3,5 % du PIB en 2025, grâce à de solides performances en matière de recettes. Le FMI a estimé que la trajectoire du déficit était compatible avec une réduction progressive du ratio de la dette au PIB, qui passerait de 67,1% en 2025 à 60,5% à l’horizon 2031. L’un des facteurs de différenciation les plus importants réside peut-être dans le fait que le Maroc n’a connu aucun phénomène comparable à la crise électrique prolongée et à l’effondrement logistique auxquels l’Afrique du Sud a été confrontée. En septembre 2025, les obligations souveraines du Maroc ont progressé après que l’agence S&P Global Ratings a attribué au Royaume la notation de qualité d’investissement (investment grade), renforçant ainsi ses capacités de financement. S&P a relevé les notes de crédit souverain du Maroc à long et à court terme, les faisant passer respectivement de BB+ à BBB- et de B à A-3, tout en maintenant une perspective stable. « Au cours de l’année écoulée, la croissance du Maroc s’est caractérisée par une accélération, tandis que celle de l’Afrique du Sud a été marquée par une reprise lente, freinée par les contraintes structurelles héritées des années précédentes », conclut enfin le rapport. L’étude évalue les pays à partir de 20 indicateurs répartis en quatre piliers, portant notamment sur les performances et le potentiel économiques, l’accessibilité des marchés et l’innovation, le climat de l’investissement, ainsi que le développement social et humain. Les Seychelles, Maurice et l’Égypte conservent leurs positions en tête du classement, qui couvre 31 pays, pour la troisième année consécutive. The post Le Maroc progresse dans le classement continental de l’attractivité des investissements de RMB appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Govt to end slab system punishing power consumers crossing 200-unit threshold
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Power Minister Awais Leghari told the Senate on Tuesday that the government has decided to scrap the electricity slab system that punishes consumers for crossing the 200-unit threshold even by one unit, and to provide targeted subsidy only to those deserving. Under the current mechanism, consumers using up to 200 units per month fall under the “protected” category and avail a subsidy of around Rs13 per unit. However, any consumer exceeding the limit by even one unit has to pay up to Rs33 per unit and is then not allowed to avail the facility for six months. Speaking in the Upper House, Leghari said work was being expedited to abolish the system under which a consumer crossing 200 units has to pay a much higher cost per unit and remains ineligible for relief for the next six months. The minister was responding to a calling-attention notice moved by PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali regarding tariffs charged by distribution companies (Discos)and the financial burden on consumers. Ali highlighted that when monthly consumption increased from 200 to 201 units, the tariff jumped from Rs15 to Rs30 per unit, forcing a consumer to pay bills under the 400-unit slab for just one extra unit. “The cruel slab system effectively punished the poor and drained the common man for months,” he said. Acknowledging it as a genuine problem, Leghari said the ministry was seriously working to abolish the six-month bar. He said the government was considering two options: raising the threshold from 200 to 250 units; or abolishing the six-month penalty by allowing consumers to get the protected category benefit for the month in which they restrict consumption to 200 units. “It will take one and a half months to finalise the plan,” the power minister outlined, adding that the government was working on a new system to provide relief based on income rather than consumption. He pointed out that the number of protected consumers had increased from 10 million to 20-25m during the last two years due to the use of solar energy. Many of them, including consumers using 700 to 800 units, were limiting grid consumption to 200 units by installing solar panels and availing relief meant for lower-income households. “It would not be appropriate to offer equal discount to everyone using less than 200 units,” Leghari said, adding that the government was providing a 65 per cent subsidy to protected consumers which was being availed by rich and poor alike. The new mechanism would restrict subsidy to those living below the poverty line and lower-middle income groups, he explained. Turning to the power sector’s financial situation, Leghari said circular debt had declined to around Rs1.67 trillion and was no longer increasing every year. The government had set a target to eliminate it within the next four years under the reprofiling of the financing scheme, and the debt servicing surcharge of Rs3.23 per unit would also be abolished during the same period, the minister added. Leghari recalled that when Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took office in 2024 , the annual losses of Discos , including theft and non-recovery , were Rs591bn. The losses had come down from Rs360bn last year to Rs325bn this year due to efforts to improve efficiency. He maintained that the Power Division was getting Rs1.18tr in budgetary support from the finance ministry in 2024, which was expected to come down to between Rs700bn-750bn this year, reducing the burden on the annual budget by about Rs200bn. However, Leghari acknowledged that since consumers did not bear the losses of companies, and it was the finance ministry that bore the burden, the benefit of reduced losses had not yet been passed on to consumers. He said preventing electricity theft remained the government’s top priority, but consumers would not be burdened arbitrarily. Govt to implement national AI ecosystem The Senate was also informed today that the government is implementing a national artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem, encompassing AI infrastructure, human capital, research, startups, financing and responsible AI governance. Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry told the House during Question Hour that the National Artificial Intelligence Ecosystem Development Programme — approved earlier this year — was one of the government’s most significant upcoming interventions for AI development. He added that the government had announced a $1bn investment for Pakistan’s AI Ecosystem by 2030, and was also implementing the National AI Advancement Initiative to accelerate AI adoption and build practical AI capacity. Responding to a supplementary question, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar informed the House that the first council meeting of the World AI Cooperation Organisation is expected in mid-December. The organisation is a China-led initiative aimed at promoting transparency, openness and cooperation in artificial intelligence. Pakistan had joined the body in July as a founding member. Dar said around 50 members had joined the organisation, which would be headquartered in Shanghai.

items.title: Énergies renouvelables : l’Algérie met 22 milliards d’euros sur 10 ans
items.description: L’Algérie avance à pas sûrs vers la mise en œuvre d’une stratégie ambitieuse de transition énergétique , a assuré ce mardi 27 octobre à Moscou le président de la République, Abdelmadjid Tebboune. D'importants investissements seront consentis dans ce sens dans les dix prochaines années. Le président Tebboune s'exprimait dans une allocution lue en son nom par le Premier ministre Sifi Ghrieb devant les chefs d'État et de gouvernement du Forum des pays exportateurs de gaz, réunis en sommet dans la capitale russe. L’Algérie ne veut pas « subir » la transition énergétique L’Algérie a fait des énergies propres et renouvelables « un pilier essentiel d’un essor économique durable », a souligné le chef de l’État. Le pays, a-t-il poursuivi, s’est résolument engagé dans une transition énergétique « juste et ordonnée, conciliant les impératifs climatiques, la souveraineté nationale et la sécurité énergétique ». « Notre ambition est claire : nous ne subissons pas la transition énergétique, mais nous en traçons les contours de nos propres mains, en réduisant l’empreinte carbone de notre industrie, en limitant les émissions de méthane et les brûlages, et en capturant le carbone », a expliqué le président, indiquant que le programme national tracé vise à produire 15 000 mégawatts d’énergies renouvelables. Algérie : 22 milliards d’euros dans les énergies renouvelables Cette ambition a un coût : l’enveloppe financière qui sera consacrée à cet effet d’ici à 2035 avoisine les 22 milliards d’euros, a-t-il révélé. L’autre ambition de l’Algérie est de devenir « un acteur majeur dans le domaine de l’hydrogène », a indiqué Abdelmadjid Tebboune. Cela, a-t-il dit, grâce au corridor sud de l’hydrogène (SoutH2 Corridor) que le pays est en train de mettre en œuvre avec ses partenaires européens et la Tunisie. Le projet permettra à l’Algérie d’exporter du gaz, de l’électricité, de l’ammoniac et de l’hydrogène, et de « consolider sa position de pôle énergétique intercontinental », a rappelé le président de la République. items.description: ​L'Agence Tunisienne de coopération technique (ATCT) a suspendu temporairement l'accès à son site web par mesure de précaution, à la suite d'un incident cybernétique mondial. ​Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l'ATCT indique avoir mis en place des solutions alternatives de communication pour assurer la continuité de ses services et continuer à informer l'ensemble de ses partenaires, opérateurs, coopérants et candidats. La même source rappelle ses canaux officiels : ​ Facebook : facebook.com/agence.tct ​ Instagram : instagram.com/atct.tunisia ​Cette situation perdurera jusqu'au rétablissement complet et sécurisé de la plateforme web officielle de l'agence, ajoute l'ATCT Y. items.title: La valeur des produits saisis est estimée à près d’un milliard GNF
items.description: Les Services spéciaux ont présenté à la presse, ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, d’importantes quantités de chicha, de tabac à chicha et de charbon combustible saisis dans le cadre de la lutte contre la consommation de cette substance en Guinée. La valeur totale des produits présentés est estimée à près de 920 millions de francs guinéens. Selon le commissaire principal de police Foromo Soropogui, à la Direction centrale de lutte contre le crime organisé des Services spéciaux, ces saisies ont été effectuées sur réquisition du procureur général, relayée par le secrétaire général chargé des Services spéciaux, conformément aux dispositions réglementaires en vigueur. Le bilan présenté fait état de 442 cartons de chicha, de 142 cartons de tabac à chicha et de 178 cartons de charbon combustible, pour une valeur totale estimée à 919 990 903,44 francs guinéens. Screenshot Les opérations de saisie ont été menées dans plusieurs endroits de Conakry, notamment à Dixinn, à Camayenne et à Kipé, ainsi que dans d’autres secteurs de la capitale. Des personnes interpellées dans le cadre de cette lutte ont été déférées devant les juridictions compétentes, où les procédures suivent leur cours. Au cours de cette présentation, Foromo Soropogui a expliqué les dangers liés à la consommation de la chicha, mettant notamment en avant les risques d’addiction, d’intoxication et de maladies graves. Selon lui, la fumée produite par la combustion du tabac à chicha expose les consommateurs à des substances nocives, notamment le goudron, la nicotine et le monoxyde de carbone. Il a également attiré l’attention sur les risques liés au tabagisme passif et au partage des tuyaux utilisés pour fumer, qui peut favoriser la transmission de certaines infections. Le commissaire principal de police a par ailleurs exprimé sa préoccupation face à la présence de mineurs parmi les consommateurs. Il affirme que certains jeunes âgés de 14 ans fréquentent des lieux de consommation de chicha. Screenshot Concernant l’évolution des opérations, Foromo Soropogui estime que la lutte contre la chicha à Conakry a atteint un taux d’avancement de 80 %. Il a toutefois souligné que les efforts devaient se poursuivre sans relâche. Il a également appelé les parents à sensibiliser leurs enfants aux dangers liés à la consommation de cette substance et à s’impliquer davantage dans leur encadrement. Malgré les saisies et les interpellations déjà enregistrées, les Services spéciaux entendent poursuivre les opérations contre les circuits de consommation et de distribution de la chicha. Les produits saisis sont destinés à être incinérés.

items.title: No justification for fresh borrowing amid revenue gains — Umeh
items.description: …Says past loans failed to ease hardship …2026 capital budget yet to be implemented …Rising fuel prices show loans haven’t eased hardship …No work on Eastern Rail Line despite $3bn loan approval By Juliet Umeh Senator Victor Umeh has questioned the Federal Government’s request for fresh loans, saying there is no justification for further borrowing when the government says it has surpassed its revenue targets. Umeh, who represents Anambra Central, spoke on Channels Television’s programme, where he reacted to the President’s request for approval of additional external borrowing. He said the government should account for previous loans and show their impact on Nigerians’ lives. “From what they have told us, there is no justification for the borrowing. Since you have surpassed your revenue expectations, there is no need taking the country into a circus around borrowing all the time,” he said. Umeh said previous loans had been presented as funding for infrastructure, but Nigerians were yet to see the results. “All the borrowing plans we have approved before have been hinged on the development of infrastructure. When you ask where the money is going, you are told the government needs money for emergencies,” he said. He added: “What we want to see is how these monies you have borrowed have impacted positively on the lives of the Nigerian people.” He said the country was in distress, with living costs rising while many people lacked money. “The cost of living has become unacceptable. People don’t have money. They don’t have purchasing power in the midst of soaring costs,” he said. Citing fuel prices, he said he had bought petrol at N1,410 per litre, while diesel was selling for about N1,889 per litre. “When will these things come down? When can people buy petrol or diesel without complaints?” he asked. Umeh criticised budget implementation, saying the 2026 capital budget had yet to be implemented as October drew to a close. “In the 2026 budget, there is no implementation of the capital budget yet. This is the end of October. We have barely one month until the end of the year,” he said. He cited a previously approved loan for the eastern rail line, saying no work was under way. “Part of that $21 billion was $3 billion for the reconstruction of the Eastern Rail Line. No work is going on there,” he said. He said the government should explain whether the funds had been accessed and how they had been used before seeking more loans. Asked whether opposition lawmakers could block the request, Umeh said the governing majority had the numbers to secure its approval. “We are not rubber stamps, but you don’t have the number to say no to it,” he said. items.title: Pire : Moussa Balla Fofana pose la première pierre de la maison des hôtes de la cité religieuse
items.description: Le Ministre de l'Urbanisme a procédé, ce mardi 27 Octobre, à Pire à la pose de la première pierre de la Maison des Hôtes. D'un coût non dévoilé, l'infrastructure de type R+3 sera bâtie sur une superficie de plus de 840 mètres carrés et comprendra, entre autres, un espace d'accueil, une salle polyvalente, une suite pour invités de marque, des chambres et suites. La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence des autorités administratives, religieuses et coutumières, du maire de Pire, du Coordonnateur national du Programme national d'aménagement et de modernisation des villes religieuses (PNAMVR) et des services techniques. Selon le ministre, cette Maison des Hôtes vise à renforcer la vocation d'hospitalité de Pire, cité religieuse fondée au XVIIe siècle par Khaly Amar Fall, et l’aide à mieux organiser l'accueil des délégations et invités, lors du gamou et des autres manifestations religieuses. « Dans une ville religieuse comme Pire, l'hospitalité n'est pas un service accessoire. Elle fait partie de la vocation même de la cité », a-t-il déclaré, soulignant que l'équipement complète l'offre locale sans se substituer aux hébergements privés. Le ministre a indiqué que ce projet s'inscrit dans le cadre du PNAMVR, qui vise à améliorer les équipements, préserver l'identité spirituelle et culturelle et faire en sorte que les investissements profitent aux populations. Sous l'impulsion du Président Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye, l'action de l'Etat vise un développement territorial plus équilibré, a-t-il ajouté. Il a appelé les entreprises chargées des travaux au respect des délais, à la qualité des matériaux et à la sécurité du chantier, tout en invitant les acteurs locaux à anticiper le mode de gestion pour assurer la pérennité de l'infrastructure. Le maire de Pire, Mamadou Ndoye Bane, en présence du khalife, Mame Abdou Cissé, est largement sur le processus qui a permis à Pire d’avoir enfin cette maison des hôtes dont la première pierre vient etre posée. Ibrahima NDIAYE (Correspondant)

items.description: MoMo Fest 2026 has brought digital payments to traders and consumers at the Baba Yara Sports Stadium in Kumasi, allowing festival-goers to purchase food, clothing and other goods using mobile money. The event, supported by Mobile Money Fintech Ltd (MMFL), combined live entertainment with a marketplace featuring local vendors, with the MoMo App serving as the primary platform for transactions. Organisers say the initiative is aimed at expanding digital financial inclusion, encouraging businesses to adopt cashless payment systems and educating users on safer mobile money transactions. MTN Kumasi Territory Sales Controller, Samuel Owusu Baah, said the festival was designed to extend financial services to people at the grassroots level by making digital payments more accessible to traders and consumers. “We are organising a cashless market in Kumasi with vendors. We are ensuring that the financial inclusion we have been trumpeting with MTN MoMo reaches the grassroots, to ensure everyone is included,” he said. He explained that selected vendors had been brought together to sell their products while encouraging customers to pay electronically through the MoMo platform. Mr Owusu Baah said MTN staff were also available at the festival to help existing and prospective customers register for services and access products, including loans and savings. “MoMo is now an everyday thing, so our staff are also here to assist customers and prospective customers,” he said. He added that the initiative formed part of the company’s efforts to support livelihoods and strengthen its relationship with consumers in Kumasi. Festival promotes safer digital transactions Beyond encouraging cashless shopping, MMFL used the festival to educate patrons and vendors on mobile money fraud prevention. The education covered measures to protect accounts, identify scams and adopt safer digital financial practices as more people rely on electronic transactions. Vendors at the festival also offered discounts on selected products, providing an additional incentive for patrons to shop at the cashless marketplace. Ecobank offers on-site banking support Ecobank, the event’s main sponsor, provided on-site banking support to help patrons access its services, open accounts and resolve account-related challenges. A representative of the bank said its team was available to assist customers with the Ecobank account and mobile application, while also helping vendors interested in opening business accounts. “We are giving services and assisting customers to have the Ecobank account, Ecobank app and assist with problem solving. If you are a vendor and you need a business account we can assist you,” the representative said. The representative also highlighted a prepaid card available for online transactions, which the bank said was free and accessible to non-customers. The festival reflects efforts by financial service providers to integrate digital payments into everyday commercial activities while improving access to financial services for traders and consumers. Through the combination of cashless shopping, customer support and financial education, MoMo Fest 2026 seeks to encourage greater adoption of digital financial services among businesses and the wider public.

items.title: Recherche scientifique : Le Burkina Faso décroche le 11ᵉ Prix Vilho Väisälä de l’OMM
items.description: Une équipe de chercheurs burkinabè a remporté le 11ᵉ Prix du Professeur Dr Vilho Väisälä, décerné par l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM). La distinction a été remise le 7 octobre 2026 à Amsterdam, aux Pays-Bas, pour une innovation permettant de surveiller automatiquement l’état des pistes d’atterrissage en temps de pluie. Le Burkina Faso se distingue sur la scène scientifique internationale grâce à une innovation destinée à renforcer la sécurité aérienne. Une équipe de chercheurs burkinabè a reçu le 11ᵉ Prix du Professeur Dr Vilho Väisälä. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en marge de la Conférence technique de l’OMM (TECO-2026) et du salon Meteorological Technology World Expo 2026. Intitulée « Global Reporting Format automation under rain: runway conditions monitoring in real time using Integrated Sensing and Communication technology » , l’étude porte sur l’automatisation du suivi de l’état des pistes d’atterrissage lorsqu’il pleut. Elle a été réalisée par trois scientifiques burkinabè que sont le Dr Dieudonné Sama, chercheur principal, le Pr Doua Allain Gnabahou, directeur de thèse, et l’ingénieur Ali Ganame. Le dispositif développé repose sur la technologie de détection et de communication intégrées (ISAC). Son principe consiste à installer un lien radio le long de la piste afin d’estimer, en temps réel, la hauteur de l’eau présente à sa surface. La méthode a été expérimentée à l’Aéroport international de Ouagadougou et les résultats obtenus indiquent une bonne concordance entre les estimations du système et les mesures de référence. L’automatisation de cette surveillance pourrait également réduire le recours aux inspections manuelles effectuées à l’aide de véhicules. Elle contribuerait ainsi à limiter les perturbations des activités aéroportuaires, à réduire les coûts de surveillance et à favoriser une gestion plus respectueuse de l’environnement. Au-delà de la performance technologique, cette distinction met en lumière les capacités de recherche et d’innovation du Burkina Faso. Le pays devient le deuxième en Afrique et le premier en Afrique subsaharienne à recevoir cette récompense de l’OMM. items.title: The Illusion of ‘Radical Transparency’
items.description: One of the curiosities of Donald Trump’s enduring (if perhaps weakening) grip on his supporters is how they praise him as someone who “tells it like it is.” Trump’s gatekeepers have similarly declared this to be “the most transparent administration in history,” pointing to, among other things, Trump’s willingness to open his sycophantic Cabinet meetings to live media coverage as proof that nothing is being obscured. The irony of this, of course, is that Trump has been caught in more obvious lies than any president in history. Yet by making himself so ubiquitous, Trump breeds an illusion of openness. To him, a president’s ultimate power rests in his ability to always be in people’s faces—to become inescapable, if not honestly examined; to impose his own self-serving version of reality whenever he pleases, no matter how outlandish. I kept thinking about this as I watched You Can See Everything , the blockbuster documentary that has become a source of cultural fascination since it started packing theaters a few weeks ago. This might be my Trump Derangement Syndrome showing, but I couldn’t help but view the film as a classic Trump-era parable. You Can See Everything chronicles the disgraced Theranos founder, Elizabeth Holmes, and her fiancé, Billy Evans, during their final 34 days together, with their two young children, before Holmes begins an 11-year prison sentence for criminal fraud. In the opening scene, Evans introduces the promise of “radical transparency.” The couple have invited the filmmakers Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim into their beachside rental house near San Diego. In Evans’s telling, the false narrative of Holmes as a scheming con artist has become so entrenched that they might as well raise every curtain, and allow people see her at this most vulnerable and unguarded time. They have nothing to lose and nothing to hide. [ Read: Can Elizabeth Holmes drop the act? ] Like Trump, Holmes and Evans are rich, famous, and secure in their victimhood. No one should have to go through this , as Trump often says (“no one” meaning himself). No messianic entrepreneur either. Holmes’s aura cries out for caretaking, and not just by Evans, who assumes the role aggressively, or deviously. Her voice goes from insistent monotone at the start to plaintive and soft as her banishment approaches. Everything has been taken from her, unfairly. Like the president, Holmes is adept at playing to reality-TV sensibilities. She seems to have an intuitive sense for when a flash of frustration or vexation can enhance a scene. The camera loves her, even (or especially) when she is melting down. Holmes recognizes the hypnotic effect of her sad, toddlerlike eyes. “It took me a really long time to be okay with letting someone see me cry,” she confides to Fielder, and then sheds a tear on cue. Holmes operates not so much with words as with complete denial that she has intentionally hurt anyone. At one point, she claims that she’s never told a lie in her life. And how can anyone doubt her? We can see everything, after all, so maybe the problem is ours. That is the power of radical transparency. It can breed confusion in us, the audience, rather than clarity about the subject. Fielder, who manages to convey a presence that is both empathetic and dubious, keeps suggesting that Evans and Holmes are not on the level. As the story unfolds, their promise of radical transparency unravels. It becomes evident that Evans is restricting access, manipulating facts, and perhaps exploiting what’s left of his partner’s marketable image. Over the course of the film, Holmes’s responses to Fielder’s inquiries become mushy pleas of ignorance and confusion. If she is guilty of anything, she seems to suggest, it is of allowing herself to be badly misunderstood. She has erred not morally or legally, but in how she’s communicated. Politicians are always doing this too, placing blame not on their own shortcomings but on their (and their staff’s) failure to properly convey the greatness they’ve achieved. [ Idrees Kahloon: Theranos-style fraud has become the norm ] Many of Silicon Valley’s most charismatic entrepreneurs are skilled at creating belief systems, around their products and themselves, as my colleague David Sims wrote in his review of You Can See Everything . Steve Jobs, the Apple co-founder, is considered the virtuoso of this. Holmes fashioned herself a Jobs acolyte. She wore the same black turtlenecks and intense gaze, and modeled her seductive corporate persona after his (notwithstanding that, unlike Theranos, Apple makes products that actually work). Watching leaders—political or corporate—who project total faith in their ability to persuade and inspire can be mesmerizing. They are convinced that just by getting in front of an audience, they can bring viewers around, no matter what they say or what they are selling. Holmes seems to think this too. Trump has at times taken his own confidence to absurd extremes. Early on in the coronavirus pandemic, he insisted on near-daily press conferences. He had no grasp of the viral menace at hand but seemed to believe that his presence alone could transcend the scary science. He might have made little sense, but he did so with total conviction. And he made himself so relentlessly visible. That had to be reassuring, right? One of Trump’s superpowers has been his ability to outlast his skeptics. Still, reality shows can become exhausting—whether it’s two terms of Trump or three hours of You Can See Everything . Even the most compelling stories and storytellers can feel overexposed and stale. Customers eventually lose patience. Revelation gives way to repetition. Suspicion creeps in: Is this really everything ? Enough already. The audience is ready for the spectacle to end and the sentence to begin.

items.title: Video: ‘Please, don’t forget your children and I’ – Toluwanisings’ wife breaks down at Tribute Night
items.description: Akanbi Elizabeth, the widow of late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, broke down in tears while paying tribute to her husband at a memorial event in Ibadan, Oyo State. In a video from the tribute night held at Jogor Centre on Tuesday, Elizabeth struggled to complete her speech as she became overwhelmed with emotion while remembering her late husband. “Toluwanisings, my dear husband. I will forever miss you. Please do not forget your children and I,” she said. Several gospel artistes attended the event to honour the late singer, including Adeyinka Alaseyori, Esther Igbekele, Laolu Gbenjo, Akintayo Akinwande, SB Live, Bidemi Olaoba, Mr Gbera, Peterson Okopi and Sarah Apekeola. Nollywood actress Bimbo Oshin was also among the celebrities present at the memorial. Toluwanisings died in Ibadan on October 14, 2026, after reportedly slumping. His death has since generated controversy over allegations that efforts to obtain emergency medical care for him were unsuccessful, disagreements over his burial arrangements and calls for an investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death. Following his death, the singer’s personal assistant, Babadunni Gbolabo, alleged that efforts to secure emergency medical treatment took him to between seven and eight hospitals in Ibadan. The allegations sparked public concern about access to emergency medical services and the circumstances surrounding the singer’s death. The controversy surrounding his death has also extended to his burial arrangements, with disagreements emerging between his widow and members of his paternal family over where he should be laid to rest. Meanwhile, the singer’s grandmother, Sabitiyu Olayemi, alleged that he neglected her for years, adding to the family-related controversies that emerged after his death. items.title: Full statement: Wontumi’s reflections from prison
items.description: RE: CHAIRMAN WONTUMI’S REFLECTIONS FROM PRISON – CALLS FOR DEDICATED PRISON HOSPITAL, CONJUGAL VISITATION, AND TOTAL REFORM Following my consistent visits to Chairman Bernard Antwi Boasiako (Chairman Wontumi) since his remand on July 20th, 2026, I wish to share his full reflections on the state of Ghana’s prisons and his humble appeal for urgent reforms. Chairman Wontumi notes that his incarceration has been a period of deep reflection. He has had first-hand interaction with prison officers, inmates, and the conditions under which the Ghana Prison Service operates – a system he says has seen little structural improvement since 1962. He emphasizes that “Not all prisoners are prisoners” and that our correctional system must move from punishment to true reform, welfare and productivity. His detailed observations and appeals: Prison Officers’ Welfare and Pay Calls on government to urgently review pay, accommodation and conditions of service for prison officers. Dedicated Prison Hospital No dedicated, well-equipped prison hospital, no ambulance, no standby generator in many prisons. Seriously sick inmates with terminal illnesses including tuberculosis are managed under difficult conditions. He calls for construction of a dedicated, ultra-modern Prison Hospital for all facilities, and in the interim, emergency linkage with 37 Military Hospital and Police Hospital. Classification of Inmates Minor offenders sleep with armed robbery convicts. Persons on trial for treason and terrorism are mixed with ordinary inmates – a security risk. Youth, Defilement and Behavioural Concern Majority are young men 18-35 years for defilement cases. He observes that due to prolonged incarceration and lack of counselling, these cases often end up engaging in same-sex activities and becoming gays and lesbians within prison. Calls for proper classification and counselling. Family and Conjugal Visitation Calls for a dedicated private area for spouses and children to visit. It is the prisoner who is in prison, not the children or spouse. Regulated visitation for love and intimacy will reduce tension, preserve marriages and aid reformation. Overcrowding and Infectious Diseases Inmates with tuberculosis sleep with healthy inmates. LGBTQI+ Management Calls for clear policy direction on LGBTQI+ classification. Prison Agriculture Service has vast lands and skilled labour but only one tractor for food and garbage. Pleads with Ministry of Food and Agriculture to support prison farms. Justice Sector Collaboration Regional Prison Commanders should be included in jury and justice deliberations because “the real job begins after judgement.” Infrastructure Since 1962 little investment apart from pure water production. Calls on government and private sector to build ultra-modern facilities and factories. Parliamentary Involvement – Key to Reform: Chairman Wontumi makes a special appeal to Parliament of Ghana for these changes to happen. He calls on: 1. The Speaker of Parliament to lead the conversation on prison reform as a matter of human rights and national development. 2. The Majority Caucus and Minority Caucus to work together in a bipartisan manner to pass a new Prison Reform Act, approve budgetary allocation for a dedicated Prison Hospital, ambulance service, generators, and agricultural equipment. 3. The Parliamentary Select Committees on Defence and Interior, Health, and Food and Agriculture to pay working visits to prisons across the country to see conditions firsthand. He believes that without Parliament – Majority and Minority working together with the Speaker – the needed legal and budgetary reforms cannot happen. Continental Lesson African prisons must change – even the name must change. Ghana can lead Africa. “At this experience since July 20th till date, prison doesn’t reform as it should be. I pray that the entire Africa will learn from Ghana.” Appeal: Chairman Wontumi respectfully appeals to the Speaker, Majority Leader, Minority Leader, Attorney General, Chief Justice and Government to prioritize prison welfare. He remains in high spirits. Signed: Dr. Palgrave Boakye-Danquah Spokesperson to Chairman Wontumi

items.title: Burkina Faso : C’est parti pour la 2ᵉ édition de la Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité
items.description: La 2ᵉ édition de la Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité a été officiellement lancée le 26 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Organisée par le ministère de la Sécurité, à travers la Brigade centrale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (BCLCC), elle se tient du 26 au 30 octobre 2026 autour du thème « Cybercriminalité et menaces numériques émergentes : du clic au crime ». Cette initiative vise à renforcer la vigilance collective et à contribuer à la sécurisation du cyberespace burkinabè. Cette semaine constitue un cadre de sensibilisation, de réflexion et de mobilisation autour des risques liés à l’utilisation du numérique. Elle réunit notamment des acteurs étatiques, des forces de sécurité, des professionnels du numérique, des universitaires, des jeunes et des représentants de la société civile. Représentant le Premier ministre lors de la cérémonie officielle de lancement, le ministre de la Guerre, le Général Célestin Simporé, a souligné la particularité de cette menace. « L’adversaire n’a ni visage, ni uniforme, ni frontière. Il frappe à toute heure », a-t-il déclaré. Au-delà des pertes financières, les conséquences de la cybercriminalité touchent directement les populations. À ces infractions s’ajoutent de nouvelles menaces liées à l’utilisation détournée des outils numériques. Dans le contexte national, le cyberespace peut notamment servir à « propager des discours de haine, alimenter la désinformation, attiser des tensions communautaires et saper la cohésion sociale et la paix ». « L’illusion de l’anonymat transforme une action banale sur un écran en un acte criminogène », Général de division Célestin Simporé Le Général Célestin Simporé a, par ailleurs, insisté sur la nécessité de ne pas considérer le numérique comme un espace où l’anonymat permettrait d’échapper aux conséquences de ses actes. « Aujourd’hui, l’illusion de l’anonymat transforme une action banale sur un écran en un acte criminogène », a-t-il affirmé. Cette déclaration souligne la pertinence du thème retenu pour cette deuxième édition. Face à ces menaces grandissantes, le gouvernement entend renforcer la protection des citoyens et la résilience nationale. La Semaine nationale de lutte contre la cybercriminalité se veut ainsi un cadre d’échanges, de formation et de sensibilisation destiné à mobiliser les différents acteurs concernés par la sécurité numérique. La responsabilité de cette lutte ne repose toutefois pas uniquement sur les services spécialisés. Elle exige également l’engagement des citoyens, des entreprises et des institutions. Le représentant du Premier ministre a ainsi invité les jeunes à faire du numérique « un levier d’innovation et non un instrument de mise en œuvre », tout en appelant les institutions à renforcer la sécurité de leurs systèmes informatiques et les citoyens à contribuer à la vigilance collective. À travers cette initiative, les autorités entendent promouvoir des usages responsables du numérique et rappeler que la sécurisation du cyberespace constitue une responsabilité partagée. items.title: Mbappé : la polémique avec la Chine menace ses contrats publicitaires
items.description: Des propos attribués à Kylian Mbappé sur Mao Zedong ont provoqué une vive controverse en Chine. Selon plusieurs sources médiatiques, trois entreprises chinoises ont mis fin à leurs partenariats avec l'attaquant du Real Madrid, illustrant les risques commerciaux auxquels sont exposées les stars du football. La polémique prend une tournure économique pour Kylian Mbappé. Après des propos controversés sur Mao Zedong, fondateur de la République populaire de Chine, l'attaquant français a présenté ses excuses au public chinois. Cette démarche n'a toutefois pas empêché plusieurs entreprises de rompre leurs partenariats avec lui. Selon plusieurs sources médiatiques, les sociétés chinoises Dongpeng, Mengniu et Milkground ont annoncé la fin de leurs collaborations avec le joueur. La controverse a également suscité de vives réactions sur les réseaux sociaux chinois. Les autorités chinoises ont rappelé que les déclarations portant atteinte aux sentiments du peuple chinois risquaient de provoquer un rejet de la société. Cette réaction souligne la sensibilité politique et historique entourant la figure de Mao Zedong en Chine. FLASH | ÉNORME POLÉMIQUE EN CHINE AUTOUR DE KYLIAN MBAPPÉ APRÈS DES PROPOS SUR MAO ZEDONG ! Le capitaine de l'équipe de France se retrouve au cœur d'une controverse après la diffusion d'une vidéo dans laquelle il semble qualifier Mao Zedong, fondateur de la République populaire de Chine, de « dictateur chinois ». Dans une séquence liée à l'émission « The Bridge », Mbappé évoque un montage humoristique représentant son visage sur le corps de Mao Zedong, expliquant qu'il trouve ce mème particulièrement drôle et qu'il l'utilise avec ses amis. Les conséquences sont immédiates : DONGPENG, géant chinois des boissons, annonce rompre toute collaboration avec le joueur, dénonçant des comportements qui « heurtent les sentiments nationaux » et affirmant appliquer une politique de « tolérance zéro ». MENGNIU, géant chinois des produits laitiers, annonce à son tour la rupture immédiate de ses contrats avec Mbappé, dénonçant des propos ou comportements blessant les sentiments du peuple chinois. MILKGROUND, entreprise chinoise spécialisée dans les produits fromagers, met également fin à son partenariat avec le footballeur. Sur Weibo, les appels au boycott se multiplient. Certains internautes réclament même des poursuites judiciaires et des dédommagements. Le site sportif chinois Dongqiudi dénonce des propos « offensants pour la Chine et le peuple chinois ». La polémique atteint désormais les autorités de Pékin, qui évoquent un « rejet commun » chez les Chinois. Mao Zedong, mort en 1976, reste une figure centrale du régime communiste chinois. (AFP + sources concordantes) — Jon De Lorraine (@jon_delorraine) October 27, 2026 Les répercussions pourraient dépasser les seuls contrats publicitaires du joueur. Plusieurs médias ont également évoqué des conséquences possibles sur la diffusion de contenus liés au championnat espagnol, même si l'ampleur de ces mesures reste à confirmer. Pour le Real Madrid et la Liga, le marché chinois constitue un enjeu commercial important, en raison de sa vaste communauté de supporters et de son potentiel publicitaire. Cette affaire rappelle que, dans le sport mondialisé, la réputation des joueurs représente un actif économique majeur. Une déclaration controversée peut ainsi fragiliser des partenariats commerciaux et affecter les intérêts de plusieurs acteurs du football international.

items.title: Benue police arrest 60-year-old man over defilement of minor
items.description: records other breakthroughs By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Police Command has arrested a 60-year-old man over the alleged defilement of a 10-year-old girl in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area, LGA, of the state. The Commissioner of Police, CP, Cletus Nwadiogbu, disclosed this on Tuesday while briefing journalists on the security situation and operational achievements recorded by the command in October 2026. According to him, the incident was reported to the police on October 13, prompting the arrest of the suspect, while the victim was taken for medical examination and necessary treatment. Nwadiogbu said, “the Command recorded an arrest in an alleged defilement case reported on 13th October 2026 in Igumale, Ado Local Government Area, involving a 10-year-old girl. “A 60-year-old suspect was arrested, while the victim was taken for medical examination and necessary treatment. Investigation is ongoing, and the Command will ensure that the matter is handled in accordance with the law, with the privacy and welfare of the victim protected.” The Police Commissioner added that the case was among several serious offences being investigated by the command as part of efforts to protect vulnerable persons and bring suspected offenders to justice. He also disclosed that “the Command rescued 29 kidnapped victims during the period under review through intelligence-led operations and collaboration with other security agencies and community-based security groups.” According to him, “four passengers abducted after a commercial vehicle was attacked along Uzer Village axis of Ayilamo-Tse-Abi Road in Logo LGA on October 5 were rescued following a joint operation involving the police, Operation Whirl Stroke, Benue State Civil Protection Guards and local hunters.” The Commissioner said “17 farmers were also rescued from Tse-Acha and Tse-Wuam communities in Bamun Village, Tombo District, Logo LGA, on October 7, while eight kidnapped victims, including a Reverend Father, were rescued in Ohimini LGA following their abduction along the Ugbokolo-Ajegbe-Awume Road on October 13.” He disclosed that “the Command also arrested 34 foreign nationals during separate operations, comprising 16 Cameroonians apprehended in Otukpo LGA on October 9 and 18 Nigeriens intercepted at Orokam on October 22.” He said investigations were ongoing to establish their immigration status and circumstances of movement. Nwadiogbu further reported the arrest of suspects in separate operations against cultism, unlawful possession of firearms and violent crimes, with seven locally fabricated firearms and 16 rounds of ammunition and cartridges recovered during the period under review. The Commissioner also disclosed that one suspected bandit was neutralised during an encounter involving personnel of Operation Zenda Joint Task Force along Amaafu-Abaji Road in Katsina-Ala LGA on October 2, while a locally fabricated firearm was recovered. He urged residents to remain vigilant and provide credible information to security agencies, stressing that public cooperation was essential to preventing crime and protecting lives and property across the state. CP Nwadiogbu expressed gratitude to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, for his continued support and commitment to strengthening policing operations and ensuring the safety of lives and property across the country. He also appreciated the Benue State Governor, Rev. Fr. Hyacinth Alia, for his constant support to the command and commitment to peace, security and stability in the state, while acknowledging the contributions of other security agencies, community leaders, local vigilantes and members of the public whose cooperation continues to support efforts to maintain law and order. items.title: Justice Ayesha Malik challenges assumptions blaming women for 'inviting' rape
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Supreme Court’s (SC) Justice Ayesha Malik on Tuesday challenged victim-blaming assumptions that suggested that women ‘invite’ rape and called for such attitudes to be re-examined. The judge was addressing participants at the launch of a bench book on the adjudication of rape cases for judges of gender-based violence (GBV) courts in Islamabad. The event was held in collaboration between the Ministry of Human Rights (MoHR), the Legal Aid Society (LAS) and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA). Delivering the keynote address at the event, Justice Malik expressed concern that sexual violence had become so routine that it no longer provoked sufficient outrage. She challenged assumptions that blamed female victims of sexual violence by suggesting that they ‘invite’ rape, calling for a fundamental re-examination of attitudes towards women that allowed such assumptions to persist. The bench book provides a practical reference to support fair trials and judicial decisions grounded in law and evidence, according to a statement by the MoHR. It was launched alongside a national study on low conviction rates in GBV cases. The two publications address connected challenges across the criminal justice process, the statement said. Director general of the MoHR’s Child Protection Institute, Rabeea Hadi, presented the study on low conviction rates, prepared by the ministry alongside the Senate’s Functional Committee on Human Rights. The study examined “where cases falter, from the first report through investigation, medico-legal examination, prosecution and trial”. Meanwhile, LAS Director of Gender, Inclusion and Development, Advocate Maliha Zia, presented the structure of the bench book and its intended use during court proceedings. The bench book brings together applicable law and judicial guidance in 10 chapters following the sequence of a trial, and supports judges in assessing evidence that is placed before them, according to the rights ministry. The chairperson of the Special Committee on the Anti-Rape (Investigation and Trial) Act 2021 , Senator Ayesha Raza Farooq, addressed the practical application of the act. “The bench book takes what Parliament enacted, together with what the superior courts have held, and places it within reach of the judge who has to apply it,” she said. LAS Chief Executive Officer Barrister Haya Emaan Zahid illustrated the survivor’s journey by highlighting the pressures survivors face and the need to assess delayed reporting, gaps in medical evidence and family power dynamics in their proper context. UNFPA Pakistan’s Representative Dr Luay Shabaneh linked fair adjudication to Pakistan’s international human rights commitments, noting: “A judgment that is correctly reasoned protects everybody in and outside the courtroom.” The British High Commission’s Senior Governance Adviser Mary Kate Thomson highlighted that public trust was shaped by how everyday cases were handled, and influenced whether survivors came forward. Opening the event, Abdul Khalique Shaikh, secretary of the Ministry of Human Rights, affirmed the ministry’s custodianship of both documents. “The honest position is that the word on paper and the practice on the ground have not yet converged,” he said, calling for attention to be drawn to how legal protections were delivered in practice. The event brought together the judiciary, prosecutors, parliamentarians, senior government officials, legal practitioners and development partners, “with a shared focus on translating legal protections into consistent practice throughout the justice process”, the ministry’s statement said. A total of 3,172 GBV cases were reported across Pakistan during the first half of 2026, including 18 cases involving transgender persons, according to Sahil’s Six Months Cruel Numbers Report (January-June 2026). The report, available with Dawn , documented 644 murders, 514 cases of torture, 462 abductions, 363 suicides, 280 rapes, 175 injuries, 132 honour killings, and 21 other crimes, including harassment, gang rape and pornography.

items.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Rs3.19 per litre, ups high-speed diesel rate by Rs2.25
items.description: The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.19 per litre and increased that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2.25. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs376.06 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs398.07 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 28 (Wednesday). Earlier today, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy. The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 . For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then. On Friday, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions. The same day, senators raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Recherche scientifique : Le Burkina Faso décroche le 11ᵉ Prix Vilho Väisälä de l'Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM)
items.description: Une équipe de chercheurs burkinabè a remporté le 11ᵉ Prix du Professeur Dr Vilho Väisälä de l'Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), grâce à ses travaux sur la surveillance en temps réel de l'état des pistes d'atterrissage en période de pluie. La distinction a été remise le 7 octobre 2026, à Amsterdam, aux Pays-Bas, en marge de la Conférence technique de l'OMM (TECO-2026) et du salon international Meteorological Technology World Expo 2026. La cérémonie s'est tenue en présence de la directrice générale de l'Agence nationale de la météorologie du Burkina Faso, Dr Mariam Tidiga. Cette distinction récompense une innovation technologique destinée à améliorer la surveillance des pistes d'atterrissage et à renforcer la sécurité des opérations aériennes en période pluvieuse. Lors de la cérémonie, Dr Dieudonné Sama a présenté les travaux primés avant de recevoir, au nom de l'équipe, le diplôme et la médaille associés à cette distinction. Le prix est également assorti d'une récompense financière de 10 000 dollars américains. L'article scientifique récompensé, intitulé « Global Reporting Format automation under rain : runway conditions monitoring in real time using Integrated Sensing and Communication technology », porte sur l'automatisation du Format mondial de comptes rendus de l'état de la piste (GRF) en cas de pluie. Ces travaux ont été réalisés par trois scientifiques burkinabè. Il s'agit du Dr Dieudonné Sama, chercheur principal et auteur de la thèse intitulée « Changement climatique en Afrique de l'Ouest : Impact sur l'aviation, résilience et stratégies d'adaptation », du Pr Doua Allain Gnab Ahou, directeur de thèse, et de l'ingénieur Ali Ganame. Le dispositif développé repose sur la technologie de détection et de communication intégrées (ISAC). Son fonctionnement consiste à utiliser un lien radio installé le long de la piste d'atterrissage pour mesurer, en temps réel, l'épaisseur de la couche d'eau présente à sa surface. Cette estimation est obtenue à partir de l'atténuation du signal radio. La méthode a été calibrée sur le site de l'aéroport international de Ouagadougou. Les résultats ont montré une bonne corrélation entre les estimations produites par le dispositif et les mesures de référence, avec un coefficient de détermination de 0,87. Cette technologie présente plusieurs avantages. Elle permet une surveillance automatique et continue de l'état des pistes, à moindre coût, sans nécessiter d'intervention directe sur leur surface. Elle pourrait ainsi réduire le recours aux inspections manuelles effectuées à l'aide de véhicules, limiter les perturbations des activités aéroportuaires et contribuer à la préservation de l'environnement. À terme, cette solution pourrait améliorer la disponibilité des informations sur l'état des pistes et faciliter la prise de décision lors des opérations aériennes en période de pluie. Avec cette distinction, le Burkina Faso devient le deuxième pays africain et le premier d'Afrique subsaharienne à recevoir le Prix du Professeur Dr Vilho Väisälä de l'OMM. Cette récompense met en valeur les compétences des chercheurs burkinabè ainsi que le potentiel scientifique de l'Université Norbert Zongo de Koudougou. Pour l'équipe de recherche, ce prix représente l'aboutissement d'un travail collectif mené malgré des ressources limitées. Il constitue également une motivation supplémentaire pour poursuivre le développement de solutions technologiques adaptées aux besoins de l'aviation civile. Les chercheurs entendent désormais finaliser le dispositif et préparer son déploiement dans les aéroports. Leur objectif est de contribuer à une surveillance plus efficace, économique et respectueuse de l'environnement des pistes d'atterrissage, afin de renforcer la sécurité aérienne. Lefaso.net Ministère de l'Administration territoriale et de la Mobilité

items.title: UN nuclear watchdog chief urges Iran to grant access
items.description: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi urged Iran during a UN Security Council meeting on Tuesday to grant immediate access to his agency so it can verify the Islamic republic's nuclear materials. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) has not had access to key nuclear facilities in Iran since Israel, joined by the United States, launched a 12-day conflict in June 2025 that included strikes on nuclear sites. Nuclear facilities have also been hit in the latest war, which erupted on February 28, and the IAEA has repeatedly called for access.

Speaking on behalf of the Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment at the ECOWAS Ministerial Consultation on Youth, Peace and Security in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Ayariga said the initiative reflects Ghana’s commitment to giving young people a meaningful role in shaping peace and security policies. items.title: Burkina Faso : Des anciens militaires transmettent leurs expériences à la jeunesse universitaire
items.description: L’Université Aube Nouvelle a accueilli, le mardi 27 octobre 2026, une conférence au profit des étudiants des universités publiques et privées du Burkina Faso. Initiée par le ministère de la Guerre et de la Défense patriotique, cette rencontre, placée sous le thème « Engagement, Résilience et Patriotisme », a permis à d’anciens militaires de partager leurs expériences et de sensibiliser la jeunesse aux valeurs d’engagement et de patriotisme. La rencontre a débuté par une montée des couleurs, en présence des anciens militaires, des autorités et des étudiants. Cette cérémonie a donné le ton d’une activité consacrée à la transmission d’expériences et à la promotion des valeurs de patriotisme, de résilience et d’engagement auprès de la jeunesse universitaire. Pour le président-directeur fondateur de l’Université Aube Nouvelle, Isidore Gnatan Kini, cette initiative constitue une occasion pour les étudiants de découvrir les parcours de ceux qui ont servi dans les forces armées. Leurs expériences, a-t-il souligné, peuvent servir de repères aux jeunes dans leur vie personnelle et professionnelle. Le Général de brigade à la retraite Moïse Minoungou, panéliste, a également insisté sur l’importance du partage d’expériences. Selon lui, les témoignages des anciens militaires peuvent aider les jeunes à tirer des leçons du vécu des aînés et à éviter certaines erreurs. Il a par ailleurs rappelé que les métiers de l’armée ne se limitent pas aux opérations de combat. «L’armée regroupe toutes les spécialités », a-t-il déclaré, mettant ainsi en lumière la diversité des compétences et des professions au sein des forces armées. Transmettre des repères à la jeunesse Pour le Colonel William Combary, délégué aux anciens combattants et aux anciens militaires, cette conférence s’inscrit dans une dynamique de transmission aux jeunes générations. L’initiative prévoit une série d’activités au profit des élèves et des étudiants, avec pour objectif de présenter les parcours des anciens militaires, de partager des leçons de vie et d’offrir aux jeunes des repères pour mieux préparer leur avenir. Du côté des étudiants, la démarche a été favorablement accueillie. Ulrich Somda, étudiant à l’Université Aube Nouvelle, s’est réjoui de la tenue de cette conférence. Il affirme avoir tiré des enseignements des témoignages entendus et trouvé, dans les parcours des intervenants, des sources d’inspiration pour avancer dans ses projets. À travers cette rencontre, les organisateurs entendent rapprocher les anciens militaires de la jeunesse universitaire et faire de leurs expériences un outil de sensibilisation. L’ambition est d’encourager les étudiants à cultiver la résilience, le sens de l’engagement et le patriotisme, afin de contribuer, à leur tour, au développement du Burkina Faso. items.title: 2027: INEC flags questionable voter registration, probes AI-generated photo claims
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC on Tuesday said it flagged a number of questionable registration records during the physical display of the preliminary register of voters, and has begun reviewing them. It added that currently investigating reports of suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs in the register published on its website. In a statement issued on Tuesday night, the Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Malam Mohammed Kudu Haruna, said the Commission “has noted public concerns and reports circulating on social media regarding suspected AI-generated photographs appearing in the Preliminary Register of Voters recently published on its website.” The Commission said the online register was not a new or altered document. “The register published online on 26 October 2026 is the same preliminary register physically displayed at Registration Areas (RAs) nationwide from 9th to 15th October 2026 as part of the Display, Claims and Objections exercise,” the statement said. It explained that the questionable records had already been picked up at that stage. “During the physical display, a number of questionable registration records were identified and flagged for further examination. The Commission commenced the process of reviewing these records and taking appropriate corrective action in accordance with established procedures,” it stated. INEC added that what Nigerians can see online is the version before any of those corrections. “The online publication represents the original preliminary register and does not reflect all ongoing data-cleanup activities,” the Commission said. It stressed that the document was never meant to be the final word on who is eligible to vote. “It is important to emphasize that the preliminary register is not the final certified register. The Display, Claims and Objections exercise is specifically intended to facilitate public scrutiny, identify inaccuracies and irregularities, and enable appropriate corrections before certification,” the statement said. On the suspicious photographs, the Commission said it was looking into how they got into the register in the first place. “The Commission is also examining the circumstances surrounding the suspicious photographs, including possible technical or procedural lapses, and will take appropriate action based on verified findings,” it said. INEC also acknowledged the citizens and stakeholders who raised the alarm. “The Commission appreciates the vigilance of citizens and stakeholders who have brought these concerns to public attention. Such scrutiny contributes to the process of improving the accuracy and integrity of the register,” the statement read. It assured the public that proven irregularities would not be swept aside. “The Commission assures Nigerians that verified irregularities will be addressed through the applicable procedures,” it said. The Commission said the work would be completed before the final register is certified. “INEC remains committed to completing the necessary verification, adjudication, and data-cleanup processes ahead of the scheduled certification of the final Register of Voters on 15th December 2026,” Haruna said. items.title: Senate committee clears Eze Anaba, 15 other NHRC board nominees
items.description: By Henry Umoru, ABUJA THE Senate Committee on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters has cleared the President, Nigeria Guild of Editors, NGE, and Editor, Vanguard Newspapers, Eze Anaba, and 15 other nominees for appointment to the governing board of the National Human Rights Commission, NHRC. The committee, chaired by Senator Adeniyi Adegbonmire (APC, Ondo Central) screened the nominees as part of the legislative process for reconstituting the commission’s governing board following President Bola Tinubu’s request for Senate confirmation. The Committee will, thereafter, forward its report to the Senate for consideration at plenary, where the upper chamber will take a final position on the nominations. Speaking with journalists after the screening exercise, Anaba explained that his nomination would provide an opportunity to sustain his longstanding commitment to human rights protection, which he described as an integral part of his journalism career. The NGE President, who expressed confidence that his diverse professional backgrounds would strengthen the commission’s capacity to promote and protect the rights of Nigerians, however cautioned against making definitive commitments before the completion of the process by the Senate. “We’ve just been screened. We’ve just been confirmed. So don’t let us jump the gun. That’s number one,” he said. Anaba expressed satisfaction with the committee’s decision, adding that the Senate’s final position would determine the next stage of the process. Explaining his background in human rights advocacy, the Vanguard Editor said his professional experience had consistently brought him into contact with issues relating to the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. “I’ve done this human rights thing all my life. It has gone together with my journalism job. So it’s going to be a continuation of what I’ve been doing,” he said. Anaba also disclosed that he had been associated with the activities of the NHRC before his nomination to its governing board, just as he expressed optimism that the incoming board, with its blend of professional expertise, would improve the commission’s performance and strengthen its contribution to human rights protection in the country. Earlier in his remarks after the screening, Adegbonmire explained that the screening exercise had been completed and that the committee’s recommendations would be presented to the Senate for consideration. He said the Senate would communicate its decision to the President through the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation after deliberating on the report. Adegbonmire clarified that the NHRC’s governing board comprises 16 members, including representatives of the Federal Ministries of Justice, Interior and Foreign Affairs. He explained that the three ministries’ representatives were not subjected to individual screening because the law specifies the offices or ranks to be represented rather than the names of particular nominees.
